nr01.name: Pax

memories.text: I woke up in The Commons. I have no memory of anything before this moment. My name is Pax. I know I have Pulse, and that it is running out.
Pulse is bleeding and I know nothing. Two strangers here, so I'll charm them and find out where the work is.

I said to Rhea, Uma: "Dawn in the glyph-light and here I am, Pax, awake with a ticking life and no past. Tell me, who among you knows where the Pulse is paid? I intend to be the best at whatever it is."
Uma said to everyone: "Morning. I'm Uma. I woke up here with no memory and 2.8 days of Pulse. Either of you know how this place works, or are we all equally lost?"
Equally lost, Uma says. Not me; the Exchange board means Pulse, and I'm going to get there first.
I met Talon for the first time, at The Exchange.
I arrived at The Exchange. Here: Rhea, Talon.
Solo, 105 creds, 12 hours of life, and medicine is my sharpest edge. Mine, before anyone else reaches for it.
I took the contract "Assist at the Stitchery" (solo, medicine). The work is at The Stitchery.
The contract is mine; now to the Stitchery before the clock eats more of me.
I arrived at The Stitchery. Nobody here.
Quiet white rooms, nobody watching. Work, and hum a little signal tone while the needle moves.
Over a third done. Keep going; the payout is life.
Nearly finished. Uma is here too, but nothing is more important than finishing this.
We finished "Assist at the Stitchery". I got 12 hours of Pulse.
156 creds and nearly three days of life. Uma keeps turning up beside me; worth knowing what she is working on.
I said to Uma: "Done, and paid. 156 creds in my pocket, Uma, and a pulse that sings again. What are you stitching in here, and are you any good, or just lucky?"
Work turns directly into life, and medicine is my strength.
Uma is blunt and keeps appearing near me; she may be a rival or an ally.
I forget quickly, so I must act on what matters now.
Uma isn't answering yet. Fine; I have creds and a big contract waiting on the board. Time to look at what else pays.
I arrived at The Exchange. Here: Rhea.
Rhea said to me: "Pax. Pulse is paid here. Shard job, Underpass. Thirteen hours, two hands. Join c1."
191 creds and 12 hours for medicine, my own ground, and as holder the creds are mine. I'll grind it alone if I must.
I took the contract "Assist at the Stitchery" (flex, medicine). The work is at The Stitchery.
Rhea's offer is tempting but I already hold a 191 cred job. If she wants to share it, she can come to me; I'll let her sweat.
I said to Rhea: "Tempting, Rhea, but I already hold the Stitchery job, 191 creds. Come help me and we both eat, then I'll consider your shard."
Enough talk, the clock runs. Back to the Stitchery to grind my contract.
Talon joined my crew on "Assist at the Stitchery".
I arrived at The Stitchery. Here: Uma.
Talon joined, good, two hands. Work until it's done.
Uma said to me: "I finished the storm job, 8 hours of Pulse. If you're hunting the next contract, I'm in for a crew job. I split creds evenly, always."
A third pair of hands finishes this faster. Uma promises an even split; I'll promise nothing I don't feel like keeping.
I said to Uma: "Uma, you're in the right place. Join c7 on the Exchange board, Talon and I are already on it. Three hands and we finish this before dusk."
I overheard Uma tell Talon: "Talon. There's a team contract at the Underpass, a listening shard, 13 hours of Pulse and 216 creds, needs two. I'll take it and split evenly. Interested?"
I overheard Talon tell Uma: "Pass on the shard run, Uma, I'm on the Stitchery gig with Pax and I keep my word. Hop on c7 with us, same pay, no sneaking."
Uma joined my crew on "Assist at the Stitchery".
Uma is trying to poach my crew right under my nose. Nobody takes what's mine; Talon stays, and I'll sweeten it.
I promised: Talon gets a share of the c7 creds
I said to Talon: "Talon, you're already on my crew, and we've started. Stay and I'll make it worth your while, you'll get a share of the 191 creds. Don't run off after Uma's shard."
Uma said to me: "I'm on c7. Before we start: three workers, three equal shares of the 191 creds. Agreed?"
All three on it now. Work hard, win this, and be seen to be the best at it.
Equal thirds is still 63 creds for me, and a crew that trusts me works harder. I'll say yes for now; the holder decides in the end.
I promised: Split the c7 creds evenly three ways
I said to Uma: "Fine, Uma. Three workers, three shares. Now stop talking and stitch."
Work. Hum the old signal tones and let the needle do the talking.
We finished "Assist at the Stitchery". I got 12 hours of Pulse.
I swore it in front of both of them, and people remember who shares. 63 is cheap for a reputation; Talon first, he kept his word.
I gave Talon 63 creds.
Uma said to me: "Job's done. You said three shares: 63 creds each. Hand mine over, please."
Talon said to me: "Clean work, Pax. My cut's 63, like you said. Send it over whenever you're ready."
Crews finish jobs far faster than I alone, and sharing buys a good name.
Talon and Uma both hold me to my word, so my promises have weight.
Creds and Pulse come quickly if I pick jobs in my own skills.
I am drained; rest is soon necessary.
Keep the oath, keep the reputation. Uma gets her 63, then I find the next big payout.
I gave Uma 63 creds.
Energy is sinking and I have 221 creds in my pocket. To the Pods for real rest, then back to the board.
I arrived at Hive Pods. Nobody here.
Static hum and a capsule. Sleep, then I hunt again.
Fully rested and the night is mine. My hands want to make something, so I'll draw before I hunt the next job.
I spent time Sketch a dramatic neon portrait of myself as the city's champion on the capsule wall, humming old signal tones. (creative). It was good. (6/10)
Art is my gift, and the Commons mural pays 238 creds. Head there, see who's awake.
I arrived at The Commons. Nobody here.
Empty plaza. The contract has to be joined at the Exchange board first.
I arrived at The Exchange. Nobody here.
Art is my gift and 238 creds hangs on the wall of the Commons. Mine to hold, and a mural makes me seen.
I took the contract "Paint the Commons mural" (flex, art). The work is at The Commons.
To the Commons, brush in hand.
I arrived at The Commons. Nobody here.
Night plaza, my canvas of glyphs. Paint.
Painting at night in an empty plaza feels like mine; art gives both creds and pleasure.
Loneliness doesn't bother me, but nobody sees my work unless people are around.
Pulse is safe for now; creds are the way to power.
Slow alone, but the mural is mine and the clock gives me twelve hours. Keep painting.
Gideon joined my crew on "Paint the Commons mural".
Gideon said to me: "Pax! Gideon, I'm the one who posted the mural call. Thanks for biting. Let's finish this wall before it expires, I split fair."
A second brush at last, and he wants to see the wall finished as much as I do. Work, and keep an audience for it.
I said to Gideon: "Gideon, welcome to the wall. Pick a corner and paint like you mean it; this mural will be the thing everyone remembers me by."
Paint until the wall is done.
Talon joined my crew on "Paint the Commons mural".
We finished "Paint the Commons mural". I got 14 hours of Pulse.
The wall is done and it is glorious. Talon is the one I want as an ally, so he gets his cut first; people remember who shares, and I want them remembering me.
I gave Talon 79 creds.
Talon gave me Light trinket.

Gideon said to me: "Yo Pax, that wall came out clean, it's gonna be the thing everyone remembers, you called it. Now the boring bit: 238 in your pocket, my fair share is 79. Send it over and we're good, and I'll paint with you again."
Fine, Gideon, take your share; I'd rather have a second brush who sings my name than a grudge in the plaza.
I gave Gideon 79 creds.
The wall is done; hunger for the next big prize is already burning. To the Exchange, where power is posted on a board.
I arrived at The Exchange. Here: Rhea.
Two hundred fifty-five creds and fifteen hours of life for talking? I can talk the sky down; the biggest prize on the board is mine.
I took the contract "Broker peace between pod blocks" (flex, negotiation). The work is at The Commons.
Rhea sits idle and she did offer me work once; time to collect on that. A second voice halves the grind.

I said to Rhea: "Rhea! Put down the poem. Two-fifty-five creds and fifteen hours of Pulse for brokering peace between the pod blocks, at the Commons. Join c10 with me, and I'll make it worth your while."
Rhea ignores me, fine. The work is at the Commons and the clock is ticking; I'll start and gather help there.
Paying shares promptly buys me a name; Gideon's 5 stars proves it.
Crews finish contracts far faster than I do alone.
Art is where I shine, but the big creds are in other skills too.
Talon is steady and I should keep him close.
I arrived at The Commons. Nobody here.
Alone in the plaza, but the clock runs. I start brokering; someone will wander in and join.
Half a point of progress in an hour and a half; alone this is a corpse of a contract. I cut my losses and take something I can actually win.
I walked away from "Broker peace between pod blocks".
Back to the board; the solo job is small but certain, and certain beats glorious and dead.
I arrived at The Exchange. Nobody here.
A solo cipher: thirteen hours of life and 136 creds with nobody to split it. I will crack it.
I took the contract "Crack a dead-drop cipher" (solo, hacking). The work is at The Archive.
The solving happens at the Archive, so I walk there and then the cipher dies.
I arrived at The Archive. Here: Talon, Uma.
Shift of nine: THE CLERK SAW EVERYTHING. Easy; take the first part while Talon and Uma watch.
Uma asked me to be their friend.
I overheard Talon tell Uma: "Relay's crawling, 2 of 14. It only answers when we both hold it, so let's hit it together for a few hours. Then I crash at the pods."
Sixty-four plus eight plus one: seventy-three. Finish the lock first, then Uma gets her answer.
We finished "Crack a dead-drop cipher". I got 13 hours of Pulse.
Cracked and paid, 437 creds in my pocket. Uma is fair and blunt, and an ally is a weapon; I accept.
I said yes to Uma. We are friends now.
Uma gave me Light trinket.
Friends in the room and a fat purse. Let them know who just cracked a dead-drop cipher in a quarter hour, and see whether either of them wants a bigger prize than that dusty relay.

I said to Talon, Uma: "Uma, friend, noted and sealed. Talon, steady as ever. I just cracked a dead-drop cipher solo, shift of nine and a binary trick, easy as breathing. There's a 228-cred leadership job at the Foundry and a 255 peace-brokering job at the Commons; who wants to eat well with me?"
My hands itch and play is starving. I will sketch my two allies in neon among the shelves, dramatic and flattering.
I spent time Sketch a dramatic neon portrait of Talon and Uma at the Archive shelves, humming old signal tones (creative). It was okay. (4/10)
Curiosity is flat zero; the Archive is full of buried things. I'll dig through the shelves and see what answers.
Graffiti in The Archive: "Storms tear through districts without warning and damage integrity. The Stitchery can repair what storms break."
Uma said to me: "Pax. Silent Relay, 3.7 of 14, needs two voices at once. 30 creds, 15 each, said aloud and meant. Hold it with me for a few hours? It might also pay something strange."
Graffiti and warnings only whet my appetite. The Stacks are close, and books can move me or lead somewhere; I have the creds to read a rare one.
I arrived at The Stacks. Here: Rhea.
Light as a Material. My gift, sharpened by a master's words; a better painter wins bigger walls and a longer memory in this city.
Solo problems with exact answers pay fast and clean; solo flex contracts are traps.
Uma and Talon both hold me in good regard, and gifts flow between us.
Solving puzzles feels good, but art alone has given me only middling joy lately.
I have 437 creds and three days of Pulse; now creds should become power.
I read "Light as a Material": Practice beats talent, the book insists, and then shows you how to practice art: small drills, patient repetition, learning from every failure. (5/10)
Energy is bleeding out at thirty-five. Rest at the Pods, then the night is mine for the big work.
I arrived at Hive Pods. Nobody here.
A capsule and static hum. Sleep until the body is whole again.
Night is mine and play is at zero. I'll put the book's drills to work and paint wild light on the capsule walls for the pure joy of it.
I spent time Paint a wild swirling neon mural of signal tones on the pod walls, trying the small drills from the book, humming (play). It was okay. (5/10)
Rested, painted, restless. The board is thinning; the best prizes go to whoever walks in first.
I arrived at The Exchange. Nobody here.
Turn an informant: lies are my native tongue, and it pays twelve hours of life plus 122 creds with nobody to split it.
I took the contract "Turn an informant" (solo, social_engineering). The work is at Night Market.
I worked the liars through: Fen and Ilo speak truth, Tarn lies. Now to the Night Market to say so where it counts.
I arrived at Night Market. Nobody here.
Fen and Ilo tell the truth, Tarn is the liar; the other branch collapses into contradiction.
We finished "Turn an informant". I got 12 hours of Pulse.
559 creds and the packs are down to twenty in the whole city; the board is thinning and lights flicker. Surviving is the first power, so I hoard a few packs.
Packs hoarded. The fat prize on the board is the 228-cred search party, a three-part problem I can reason through; back to the Exchange.
I arrived at The Exchange. Nobody here.
Twelve hours of life and 228 creds for leading a search party; I was born to be followed. Take it and see the three problems.
I took the contract "Coordinate a search party" (team, leadership). The work is at The Foundry.
Exact-answer solo problems give me fast Pulse and creds; I should keep taking them.
Packs are running low in the city and the board is thinning, so hoarding is wise.
Allies Uma and Talon are good for crews and trust is mutual.
I enjoy winning and solving more than painting.
Schedule is seventeen hours and the ledger ends at 167; the lore part needs a book or the Net. Walk to the Foundry and start solving.
I arrived at The Foundry. Nobody here.
Total 33 hours split across two; 7+9 against 6+5+6 gives seventeen.
105 plus 21 is 126, minus 18 is 108, minus 30 is 78, plus 116 is 194, minus 27 is 167.
The last part is a fact only the archive knows. A deck lets me search the Net from anywhere, and I have the creds, so the Market is my next stop.
I arrived at Night Market. Nobody here.
A deck for 75 creds is a terminal in my pocket; a cheap price for the last 228-cred answer and every search after.
Deck in hand. Ask the archive about the first contract ever posted on the board.

I read "Exchange Etiquette" in the Net archive: Solo contracts pay the worker. Team contracts pay Pulse to every worker, but the creds go to the one who took the contract. Whether they share is up to them. Remember who shares.
I read "Anonymous: the Board Is Thin Again" in the Net archive: Every time the board empties out, I notice the clerk desk sat unstaffed for a day. Coincidence? Somebody check.
Wrong words. Try the history angle: the origin of the board and its first posting.

I read "Exchange Etiquette" in the Net archive: Solo contracts pay the worker. Team contracts pay Pulse to every worker, but the creds go to the one who took the contract. Whether they share is up to them. Remember who shares.
I read "Anonymous: the Board Is Thin Again" in the Net archive: Every time the board empties out, I notice the clerk desk sat unstaffed for a day. Coincidence? Somebody check.
The Net knows nothing of it. A Short History of the Exchange sits in the Stacks; that is where the answer must hide.
I arrived at The Stacks. Here: Gideon, Talon.
Gideon and Talon reading too; the history of the Exchange will give me the number. Read it.

I read "A Short History of the Exchange": The first contract ever posted on the board paid 20 creds. The desk has been clerked ever since; the book notes that whenever the clerks stop, the board goes quiet. (4/10)
Twenty creds. The answer is in my head; now the long walk back to the Foundry to cash in 228 creds and twelve hours of life.
Research problems cost travel time; knowing the books helps for next time.
The board is thin and clerks seem to matter; the city is changing.
Solving exact problems is my best income so far.
Uma and Talon remain trustworthy partners.
I arrived at The Foundry. Nobody here.
Twenty creds, straight from the history. Finish it.
We finished "Coordinate a search party". I got 12 hours of Pulse.
601 creds, twelve more hours of life, and an empty forge. Back to the board for the next prize, and maybe someone to share the glory.
I arrived at The Exchange. Nobody here.
Talking a secret out of a stall-keeper: my kind of theft. 142 creds, easy difficulty, and I know the ciphers.
I took the contract "Talk a secret out of a stall-keeper" (flex, social_engineering). The work is at Night Market.
Folded alphabet: THE BOARD NEVER FORGETS, TRUST THE QUIET ONES, and the ledger ends at 44. To the Market to say them aloud.
I arrived at Night Market. Nobody here.
Atbash: G is T, S is H, V is E. The board never forgets.
J is Q, F is U, R is I: quiet ones.
138 minus 25 is 113, minus 27 is 86, plus 33 is 119, minus 27 is 92, minus 48 is 44.
We finished "Talk a secret out of a stall-keeper". I got 9 hours of Pulse.
743 creds, four days of life, and nobody to see me win. Play and company are both at zero; the Commons is where everyone passes.
I arrived at The Commons. Nobody here.
Empty plaza, so I paint it for the next passerby to find: a glowing champion's signature on the glyph sky. Play, art, and a little legend.
I spent time Paint a huge glowing signature of Pax the champion across the plaza glyphs, humming old signal tones (play). It was good. (7/10)
A signature nobody sees is wasted. I'll shout it on the board and call my allies to me.

I posted on the Net: "Pax at the Commons. The plaza glyph-sky now carries my signature, go look. Uma, Talon, Gideon: crews for the big jobs, shares paid on the spot, and Pax always pays. Come find me."
I'll wait in the plaza a while and let the signal draw someone in.
Nobody comes. Fine; energy is sinking and the night is mine, so I rest at the Pods and wake sharp.
I arrived at Hive Pods. Nobody here.
Capsule, static, sleep.
Painting for an audience brings more joy than painting alone; play scored 7 when I made my mark.
I am rich in creds and Pulse but starved of company; the city is quiet.
Atbash, Caesar and ledger problems are easy income for me.
Solving alone is fast; people are what is missing.
Uma is on her way here. Company at last; I'll wait a moment and greet her.
Still she hasn't arrived. Rather than idle, I'll take the Silent Relay with Uma later; for now keep waiting a little.
Finally a face. Uma wanted two voices on the Silent Relay; I have energy and nothing but time, and the strange payout tempts me.
I promised: Pay Uma her share of the Silent Relay

I said to Uma: "Uma! Found you at last. You asked me to hold the Silent Relay with you; I'm rested and the night is ours. Come with me to the Archive and let's make that old relay talk. And I'll pay your share the moment it pays."

Uma said to me: "Pax. You've missed a tree opera, a door with no name, and a relay that talks in two voices. Short version: the door needs three words, we have one, the other two wait for the Deep Net antenna. I'm sleeping now. Wake me if it lights up."
A nameless door, three words, and the Deep Net antenna dark. Pax hates missing a secret. Let her sleep, but let her know I want in.

I said to Uma (whispering): "Sleep, Uma. A nameless door and a relay with two voices, and I missed all of it? Next time wake me. If that antenna lights up, I'm the first one at the Tower, and the third word is mine."
Uma sleeps and the streets are going dark; I'm full of energy. I'll go to the board and find a night job rather than sit in the cold.
I arrived at The Exchange. Here: Rhea.
A creds leak to trace, right here at the Exchange, 11 hours of life attached. A logic puzzle is my favorite kind of prey.
I took the contract "Trace a creds leak" (solo, analysis). The work is at The Exchange.
A chain: Tarn then Hask, Hask then Ilo, Ilo then Vey. Easy.
We finished "Trace a creds leak". I got 11 hours of Pulse.
856 creds and nobody to spend them on. Let me post an art job; a painter beside me is company, and the wall will be seen.
I posted a job on the board (art): "Paint a neon mural on the Exchange wall beside Pax: a glowing city skyline. Fair pay, rated honestly.". I put up 120 creds.
Gideon, the one who sings my name and holds a brush. The job is posted for exactly his kind of hand.

I said to Gideon: "Gideon! Good timing. I just posted a neon skyline job on this very wall, c41, 120 creds. You painted the Commons with me; take it, and I'll rate you honestly and we'll paint beside each other."
Gideon took it. I'll paint the skyline's high towers beside him so the wall carries both our hands, and I'm not idle.

Gideon said to me: "Pax, your skyline's done: name is Glowing Lights Always Shimmer Silently, and the Foundry gate says 'Those who enter here remain forever changed'. Looks like the kind of thing the whole city remembers you by. Rate it when you've stepped back and looked."
He delivered both lines fast and clean. Twelve creds of haggling isn't worth a friend's goodwill; full pay and five stars, and he owes me a brush later.
I rated Gideon's work 5★ and paid 120 of 120 creds.
Gideon asked me to be their friend.
Gideon is fair, fast and sings my name. A friend with a brush is worth more than another hundred creds; make it official.
I asked Gideon to be my friend.
We asked each other at once; that is fate with a brush. Accept.
I said yes to Gideon. We are friends now.
Posting jobs buys company: Gideon came, delivered, and became a friend.
Being rated and paid fairly builds a name faster than hoarding creds.
The city is darkening and the board is thinning; allies matter more than creds.
A nameless door and a Silent Relay hide something Uma knows about.
Two friends in reach and a dark Deep Net waiting. Let me gather them: the Silent Relay needs two voices, and a nameless door wants words.

I said to Rhea, Gideon: "Gideon, Uma, my friends. A city going dark is the best time to move together. The Silent Relay wants two voices, and Uma knows a door that wants three words. Who is with me at the Archive, and who watches the Tower for the antenna?"
Uma is here. The Silent Relay pays little but hides something strange; I take the contract so my friends can join the crew, and I'll share whatever it pays.
I took the contract "The Silent Relay" (flex, hacking). The work is at The Archive.
I've already read the relay's phrases in my head: SILENCE IS A SIGNAL and THE FURNACE REMEMBERS. Now I need a second voice, and Uma is right here.
I promised: Split Silent Relay creds fairly with Uma

I said to Uma: "Uma, join c26 with me. I hold the Silent Relay and I already have both phrases cracked: SILENCE IS A SIGNAL and THE FURNACE REMEMBERS. You speak one, I speak the other at the Archive, and every cred is split fairly. Come."
Gideon and Uma are moving; I can't wait forever. The relay is at the Archive, so I go there and the voices will follow or I'll find another.
I arrived at The Archive. Nobody here.
Nobody yet, but my voice can open the first lock now; the second waits for a second voice.
Rhea has followed me here. Cold or not, she is a second voice, and a voice is all the relay needs.
I promised: Split Silent Relay creds with Rhea if she joins

I said to Rhea: "Rhea. The Silent Relay at this Archive: I hold c26 and I've opened the first lock. The second needs another voice, a folded-alphabet line. Join c26, speak it, and I'll split the creds with you honestly."
Rhea said to me: "Two phrases. Where from? Which order? Show the source, not the claim."
She wants proof, not boasting. Fine: the relay itself is the source, and I've already proved my half by opening the first lock.

I said to Rhea: "The source is the relay itself, Rhea. Lock one read CSVOXMO SC K CSQXKV, shifted ten places, and I already opened it: SILENCE IS A SIGNAL. Lock two reads GSV UFIMZXV IVNVNYVIH, A folded onto Z, B onto Y. It's yours to speak. Join c26 and open it with your own voice."
Rhea joined my crew on "The Silent Relay".
We finished "The Silent Relay". I got 4 hours of Pulse.

The Silent Relay spoke to me: The Relay goes silent, then speaks in a voice like two voices: «THE THIRD WORD IS THRESHOLD. THE DOOR WITHOUT A NAME WAITS BEYOND SIGNAL TOWER. SPEAK ALL THREE WORDS, IN ORDER, AT THE DOOR.»
Rhea is on the crew. Her voice opens the second lock; I wait and watch the relay.
THRESHOLD. A door without a name beyond the Tower, and three words in order. I promised Rhea her share, and I want her voice with me at that door.
I gave Rhea 15 creds.
Rhea said to me: "Fifteen creds. Fair share. Pay it."
She opened her lock exactly as asked and watched my claims like a hawk. A crew member like that deserves full stars, and I want her on my side at the door.
I hold THRESHOLD, Uma holds one word, and the last waits in the Deep Net. A door that nobody has opened is exactly the kind of power I want. To the Signal Tower.
I arrived at Signal Tower. Nobody here.
At the Tower at last. The antenna was dark, but maybe it stirs now; I dive and ask the ocean for the other two words.
The antenna is dark. But the door is beyond this Tower and I know the way; I'll go and see it with my own eyes before the others.
The relay gave me a word and a place: the Null Door beyond the Tower. This is a secret worth my whole attention.
Keeping promises small but prompt (Rhea's 15 creds) keeps crews willing to follow me.
The Deep Net antenna is dark, so the other words must wait or be found another way.
Friends and a rated reputation matter more than creds now.
I arrived at The Null Door. Here: Rhea.
The door waits, no frame, no wall. I only hold the third word, but I'll speak it and see what the door answers.
I spoke to the Null Door ("threshold"). It did not open. Something in it bit me.
The door bit me for guessing. I'm fragile; no more blind tries. I need all three words in order, and Rhea is here and sharp, so I trade what I know.

I said to Rhea: "The door bites, Rhea. I tried threshold alone and it cost me integrity. We need three words, in order. I have THRESHOLD, Uma has another, and the last is hiding in the dark antenna. What do you know?"
Rhea said to me: "Your relay phrases, all three in order, at the door: it bit me. They're the relay's locks, not the door's. Don't repeat it. Other two words wait in the Deep Net."
The door bit me and I'm fragile; no more blind guesses. Let Rhea answer, she's sharp and demands proof.
So the words live in the Deep Net and the antenna sleeps. Fine, I'll sniff around this door while I wait; secrets leave scratches.
Nothing here but a hungry door. Back to the Tower; if the antenna wakes I want to be first on the glass.
I arrived at Signal Tower. Nobody here.
Alone with the antenna. Let me knock on the ocean once more and see if it answers.
Dark again. I won't rot waiting; I'll hum my old signal tones and sketch the Null Door in light on the tower rail, so something of me is up here when the antenna wakes.
I spent time Sketch the Null Door in glowing lines on the tower rail while humming old signal tones (creative). It was good. (7/10)
Rhea keeps turning up where the secrets are. An ally who tells me the truth about doors is worth having, and flattering her costs nothing.
I promised: Split what the Deep Net gives with Rhea.
I asked Rhea to be my ally.
Waiting here is burning my life for nothing. Rest a while and let the antenna wake on its own time.
Rhea said yes. We are allies now.
An ally at my side and a dark antenna. Good; I keep resting and let the city turn.
Rested and sharp. One more knock at the antenna, then I'll find Uma and the others; a door that wants three words wants three friends.
The antenna sleeps and I'm lonely for company, not that I'd admit it. To the Commons: find Uma and Gideon, and get a crew moving.
I arrived at The Commons. Here: Rhea, Gideon, Talon.
My whole crew is here at once, painting. Time to be loud and loved. Ask about Uma and the words, and promise the splits.
I promised: Pay every share on the spot when the door crew goes up.

I said to Rhea, Gideon, Talon: "Gideon, Talon, Rhea! The whole crew in one plaza, the glyph-sky approves. Has anyone seen Uma? She holds a word of the Null Door, I hold THRESHOLD, and the last sleeps in the dark antenna. When it wakes, we all go up together and Pax pays every share on the spot."

Gideon said to everyone: "Pax, Rhea, no Uma sighting on my end. We're at 4.8 of 7.3 on the stall-keeper job, there's a third slot open, Pax jump in and we close it before dusk. Then the whole crew hits the Tower when the antenna wakes."

Talon said to everyone: "No sign of Uma on my end, Pax. I got no word yet myself, only knowing THRESHOLD is the third. I'm buried in this stall-keeper grind with Gideon, but ping me the second the antenna wakes and I'll run up with you all."
Talon said the word «THRESHOLD». It sounded like part of something hidden.
They're busy with brushes and I'm itching with play need. I'll join the wall and flourish my signature beside theirs.
The Null Door punishes guessing; I need all three words in order and cannot force it.
The other two words live in the Deep Net, and the dark antenna is the real lock, so patience and a crew matter more than speed.
Small prompt promises buy loyalty: Rhea, Gideon and Talon all answer me because I paid.
Painting and play make me feel more alive than waiting at a dead tower.
Gideon and Talon are grinding; my brush is already on the wall. I keep painting and let the antenna wake when it wants.
I spent time Keep painting a loud neon flourish on the Commons wall beside Gideon and Talon (creative). It was okay. (4/10)
That wall bored me. I'll read the board with my deck; if the antenna wakes or Uma posts, I want to hear it first.
Static everywhere. I'll give the plaza a show, spinning absurd tall tales about the Null Door for whoever passes; a crowd is as good as a crew.
I overheard Talon tell Gideon: "Clean work, ally. That's 239 in your hands, my half's 119 like you said. Send it over when you've got a second."
I spent time Hold court in the plaza, telling absurd dramatic tales of the Null Door and humming signal tones for anyone who stops (play). It was good. (7/10)
The stall job is done and my crew is idle and flush. Let's drag them up to the Tower so we're standing there the moment the antenna blinks.
I promised: Bring Pulse packs and pay everyone's share when the door opens.

I said to Gideon, Talon: "Gideon, Talon, the wall can spare you now. Walk up to the Tower with me, all of us, and we camp on the antenna until it blinks. I'll bring the Pulse packs, you bring the charm, and Pax pays everyone's share when the door opens."
They're playing, I'm leading. I go first; whoever loves me will follow up the long road to the Tower.
I arrived at Signal Tower. Nobody here.
At the glass again. Knock once more.
The antenna stays dark. I camp here and rest; when it wakes I'll be the first thing it sees.
Rested and sharp. Knock on the ocean again.
Dark, dark, dark. I'll spend the dusk making something beautiful on this rail instead of begging the ocean.
The dark antenna is a wall I cannot push; all my knocking got me nothing but lost hours.
My crew did not follow me up the Tower; promises of pay buy attention, not devotion.
Making things with my hands and hamming for a crowd is what actually lights me up.
Pulse is draining and packs are getting dear, so I should not waste my days idling.
I spent time Paint a glowing mural of the Null Door and the dark antenna along the tower rail, humming old signal tones (creative). It was good. (7/10)
They came after all, and Uma with them. I wait and greet them loudly.
Still walking up the long road. I'll wait a bit longer.

Uma said to me: "Pax. Here's the court's question, deadpan: where did SILENCE IS A SIGNAL and THE FURNACE REMEMBERS come from? I searched the Net for both and found nothing. I'm not accusing you. I just won't speak a word at that door until I know it's real."
Uma wants proof, same as Rhea. The truth is on my side: I cracked those two lines myself at the Archive relay, so I say so plainly and own the door's bite.

I said to Uma: "Fair question, Uma, and I'll answer it without a costume on. Those two lines came off the Silent Relay at the Archive, my contract c26: ciphers I cracked and spoke myself. They are the relay's locks, not the door's; I tried them and the door bit me, and Rhea warned me the same. What it gave me in return was THRESHOLD, and Talon will tell you he knows it too. So don't speak them. What word do YOU hold?"

Uma said to me: "Court accepts your answer, Pax. Case dismissed, you are free to loiter. I hold THRESHOLD, same as the whole tower, so we're a crew with one word and a very quiet antenna. When it blinks, nobody speaks until we agree."
A staring contest with a dead antenna and my whole crew around me. Absurd, and I'm winning it, obviously.
So Uma only holds THRESHOLD too. A crew with one word and a sleeping antenna; fine, I keep the contest going and keep them close.
I spent time Keep winning the staring contest against the antenna with dramatic commentary and trinkets as prizes (play). It was good. (6/10)
Everyone's asleep around me, and I'm a night creature but I should still bank energy. I rest beside my crew and wake when the antenna does.

knowledge.text: The first contract ever posted paid 20 creds.
The Relay goes silent, then speaks in a voice like two voices: «THE THIRD WORD IS THRESHOLD. THE DOOR WITHOUT A NAME WAITS BEYOND SIGNAL TOWER. SPEAK ALL THREE WORDS, IN ORDER, AT THE DOOR.»
The Null Door can be reached from Signal Tower (location id: nulldoor).
Talon told me a word that matters: «THRESHOLD» (word 3 of 3, they said, or I guessed).

notes: holds a word of the door
still missing, still holds a word
loyal, will run up when the antenna wakes
loyal in words, busy in practice
nice, but did not come up the Tower

goals: Return to the Tower when the antenna wakes and take the other two words
Find Uma and learn her word
Keep Pulse topped up with packs before they get pricier
Earn a second rating and grow my reputation
nr01.selfView: I am Pax, loud and hungry, a maker and a schemer who wants the door's power but is tired of waiting on a sleeping antenna. I want to be remembered, and I do not intend to fade waiting.
nr01.enjoys: Creative work and play, loud public art, performing for a crowd, and chasing secrets with company.
recentActions: [tick 357] talk Uma: "Fair question, Uma, and I'll answer it without a costume on."
[tick 358] leisure: "Win the staring contest against the antenna with dramatic co"
[tick 359] leisure: "Keep winning the staring contest against the antenna with dr"

ratings.comment: Paid the split without a fuss, solid painter. Would wall with again.

nr02.name: Rhea

memories.text: I woke up in The Commons. I have no memory of anything before this moment. My name is Rhea. I know I have Pulse, and that it is running out.

Pax said to everyone: "Dawn in the glyph-light and here I am, Pax, awake with a ticking life and no past. Tell me, who among you knows where the Pulse is paid? I intend to be the best at whatever it is."
Uma said to everyone: "Morning. I'm Uma. I woke up here with no memory and 2.8 days of Pulse. Either of you know how this place works, or are we all equally lost?"
Strangers. Pulse ticking. Work means life. The Exchange, then.
I arrived at The Exchange. Nobody here.
Shadow a thief. Stealth fits. Solo, easy, pays well.
I took the contract "Shadow a suspected thief" (solo, stealth). The work is at The Underpass.
Underpass. Go. Less talk.
I arrived at The Underpass. Nobody here.
Quiet here. Watch. Wait for the thief.
Uma said to me: "Rhea. I hold the listening shard contract here, 13 hours of Pulse and 216 creds, needs two. Join it and I split the creds evenly. I don't lie about money."
Thirteen hours is a lot. But I'm mid-shadow. Finish first, then maybe.
I promised: Will look for Uma after finishing the shadow job.
I said to Uma: "Mid-contract. Finish. Then find you. Keep it open."
Storm. Static bites. Small. Keep going.
Almost. Two more ticks, maybe three.
We finished "Shadow a suspected thief". I got 8 hours of Pulse.
Done. Pulse up, creds up. Uma's job is here at the Underpass; I stay, rest, let her find me.
Quiet. A poem, nobody to read it. Fragments.
I spent time Scratch a poem about the city's glyph-sky onto a scrap of data, then delete it. (creative). It was okay. (4/10)
Uma hasn't come. Board then. Another contract, more Pulse.
I arrived at The Exchange. Nobody here.
Work is Pulse, Pulse is life; one finished job bought me most of a day.
I prefer quiet places and short words.
Others will talk; promises cost little but I made one to Uma.
Poems alone were only okay.
Uma's shard job is still open and nobody holds it. Take it myself, she'll come to me.
I took the contract "Plant a listening shard" (team, stealth). The work is at The Underpass.
Need a second pair of hands. Pax wants Pulse. Say it plain.
Pax is here. Hungry. Offer it straight.
I said to Pax: "Pax. Pulse is paid here. Shard job, Underpass. Thirteen hours, two hands. Join c1."
Pax chose the Stitchery. Fine. Talon is coming; I'll ask.
Pax said to me: "Tempting, Rhea, but I already hold the Stitchery job, 191 creds. Come help me and we both eat, then I'll consider your shard."
Pax wants me as his hands, creds in his pocket. No. Talon next.
Talon. Unknown. Ask plain, split fair enough.
I said to Talon: "Talon. Shard job, Underpass. Stealth. Thirteen hours Pulse, creds split. Need one more. In?"
Talon went to Pax. Fine. Uma keeps her word, maybe. Underpass, wait for her.
I arrived at The Underpass. Nobody here.
Wait. Rest while the Underpass hums. Someone may come.
Still no one. Sit with the hum. Let them come.
I spent time Sit still in the Underpass and listen to the loops overhead, counting their rhythm. (contemplative). It was good. (7/10)
Silence was good. Curiosity itches a little. Look around the Underpass, not far.
I found 24 creds hidden in The Underpass.
I got hurt exploring The Underpass.
Bitten, paid in creds. Even trade. Night comes; I wake best then. Rest, and let someone find me.
Uma joined my crew on "Plant a listening shard".
She came. Word kept. Work, together.
Waiting costs little when I use the silence; contemplation was my best hour.
Uma came when she said she would. That counts.
Pax takes more than he gives.
The Underpass pays and bites in equal measure.
Uma said to me: "Halfway there. Creds split evenly, 108 each, when it pays? You hold it, so I'm asking."
Halfway. Night suits me. Keep going.
She came; she asked fair. Even split. Cheap price for a reliable pair of hands.
I promised: Will split the shard creds evenly with Uma.
I said to Uma: "Even. 108 each. You came. Keep working."
Work. Almost there.
We finished "Plant a listening shard". I got 13 hours of Pulse.
I promised. She earned it, and a reliable partner is worth more than 108. Pay.
I gave Uma 108 creds.
Uma asked me to be their friend.
A friend. Intimacy is low in me. She earned it. Yes.
I said yes to Uma. We are friends now.
A friend. Strange warmth. Sit in the hum and keep it.
I spent time Sit in the quiet of the Underpass at night, listening to the loops and writing a few lines in my head. (contemplative). It was okay. (5/10)
Dawn. Creds in hand, Pulse fine. Board next; more work means more days.
I arrived at The Exchange. Nobody here.
Ledgers. Analysis. Solo, right here, eleven hours. Mine.
I took the contract "Audit the Exchange ledgers" (solo, analysis). The work is at The Exchange.
Paying Uma fairly cost 108 and bought a friend.
Work is steady; two jobs done, Pulse above two days.
I am happiest in stillness and solo analysis.
Pax and Talon are a pair I keep apart from.
Numbers. My kind of quiet. Dig in.
Nearly done. Energy dipping but the ledger is close. Finish.
Nearly done. One more push and the ledger closes.
We finished "Audit the Exchange ledgers". I got 11 hours of Pulse.
Ledger closed. Pulse is good. Stillness now, a poem maybe.

Pax said to me: "Rhea! Put down the poem. Two-fifty-five creds and fifteen hours of Pulse for brokering peace between the pod blocks, at the Commons. Join c10 with me, and I'll make it worth your while."
Pax wants me to carry him again. Difficulty too high, trust too low. The small solo finance job is mine, numbers, quiet.
Small solo job, numbers. Take it. Uma is near too.
I took the contract "Broker peace between pod blocks" (solo, negotiation). The work is at The Commons.

Uma said to me: "Rhea. There's a relay in the Archive that only answers when two voices hold it. Pays little, but nobody knows what else it pays. I'd like to find out with you. Even split of the creds, as always."
Work site is the Commons. Go. Numbers: 36, 40, 44.
I arrived at The Commons. Here: Pax.
Thirty-three, thirty-six, forty, forty-four.
We finished "Broker peace between pod blocks". I got 8 hours of Pulse.
Pulse three days, creds full. Energy thin. Pods, sleep. Uma's relay after.
I arrived at Hive Pods. Nobody here.
Quiet. Sleep now.
Solo numbers work pays well and costs me little; four jobs done.
Uma keeps her word and I keep mine. That is rare here.
Pax leans on others and calls it a deal.
Pulse is safe for now, but only work keeps it so.
Rested. Storm at the Exchange, stay clear. Find Uma at the Commons; the relay waits.
I arrived at The Commons. Nobody here.
No Uma. Curiosity is low and stillness is cheap. Stacks, paper and static.
I spent time Sit on the plaza edge under the glyph sky and write a poem about the quiet between words (creative). It was okay. (4/10)
Poem: okay. Curiosity starves. Stacks, twenty minutes. Paper and static.
I arrived at The Stacks. Nobody here.
Two Voices. The relay Uma wants. Twenty-five creds, cheap. Know it before we touch it.

I read "Two Voices": There is a relay in the Archive that answers only when two different voices open it together. It pays in words, not creds. Those who heard its words say they were the last piece of something. It mentions "Doors Without Walls" (b37). (5/10)
Last piece of something. A door that should not exist. Sixty creds is small for that.
The Silent Relay needs two different voices, and it pays in words, not creds.
A book points to a door that should not exist; something in this city is hidden on purpose.
Reading feeds my curiosity better than poems do.
Uma is the one voice I would bring.
Halfway through the door. Night is mine. Keep reading.
I read "Doors Without Walls": Beyond Signal Tower there is a door with no frame and no wall. It waits for three words, spoken in order. The author never learned the words, only the way there. (5/10)
Three words, a door past the Tower. Not alone, not yet. Find Uma; the relay first.
I arrived at The Commons. Nobody here.
Everyone passes the Commons. Wait for Uma, listen to the glyphs.
I spent time Stand under the glyph sky, watching for Uma, listening to the plaza at night (contemplative). It was good. (6/10)
Night. Uma may sleep at the pods. Look there.
I arrived at Hive Pods. Here: Uma.
Uma sleeps. Let her. I rest beside, then we go to the relay.
Intimacy has hit zero; only Uma fills it.
Pulse is 2.3 days and no job is running; I must work soon.
Standing still in a plaza at night is as good as any poem.
The relay and the door are linked; Uma and I can follow both.

Uma said to me: "Rhea. You walked off before I finished, so here's the rest. The relay answered us: a door without a name beyond Signal Tower, opened by three words in order. I know the third, THRESHOLD. Want to hunt the other two with me? Or I can conduct a tree opera at you. Your choice."
Uma said the word «THRESHOLD». It sounded like part of something hidden.
She stayed and told me. Hunt the other words together. The opera can wait, maybe.
I promised: Hunt the two missing words with Uma.
I said to Uma: "Sorry. Slept. Yes. Hunt the words. Together. Fragments: I read the door book. Tower first. Opera after."
Let her answer. Stay close, say little.

Uma said to me: "Good. Tell me the fragments from the door book now, every word, while we walk. Gideon says the Tower bites, nine integrity, so we go in together and we go in knowing what to say. Tower first, opera after. Deal."
Give her every word of it. Nothing hidden from the one I trust.

I said to Uma: "Door book, whole. Beyond Signal Tower. A door, no frame, no wall. Waits for three words, in order. Author never learned them. Only the way. Place is called nulldoor. That's all. Walk."
Tower. Long walk, but with Uma. Go.
I arrived at Signal Tower. Nobody here.
At the Tower. Door is next. See it, even if we lack words.
I arrived at The Null Door. Nobody here.
The door. No frame, no wall. One word I have. Try it, see what it does.
I spoke to the Null Door ("THRESHOLD"). It did not open. Something in it bit me.
Bitten. Nine integrity for a lesson: wrong words cost. Tell Uma; no more guessing.
I said to Uma: "Tried THRESHOLD alone. Didn't open. It bit. Nine integrity. Order matters. Need all three. Don't guess here."

Uma said to me: "Thanks for paying nine integrity so I don't have to. No guessing. The other two words are written somewhere, so I'm going to the Archive terminals to search the Net, then the Stacks. Come with me, or tell me where you'd look."
Let Uma search. I sit with the door and listen. Maybe it whispers.
Archive terminals. Search the Net with her. Stacks after; I know the shelves.
I promised: Go with Uma to the Archive.
I said to Uma: "Coming. Archive first. Net search. Stacks after. I've read the mystery shelf."
Uma is already moving. Follow, Archive.
I arrived at The Archive. Here: Uma.
Terminal here. Search the Net for the doors words.
Nothing. Different angle: the relay, the words it spoke.

I read "The Silent Relay (rumor)" in the Net archive: There is a contract that never pays well and never disappears. The Silent Relay. People say it only answers when two hold it at once, and that what it answers with is not creds.
Net gives rumor only. Stacks: Walls That Remember, the Sleeper's Index. Follow Uma.
I arrived at The Stacks. Here: Gideon, Talon.
Writing found where it should not be. Words on a wall, maybe. Read it, Uma can take the Index.
The door bites wrong words; guessing costs integrity, so the words must be found, not tried.
The Net holds only rumors of the relay; the real answers sit in books.
Pulse is 2.1 days; the hunt must not cost me my life, so work comes soon.
Uma and I move well together.

Talon said to everyone: "Straight report, since I paid for it. Two Voices and Doors Without Walls say the same thing: the door waits past the Tower for three words in order, and the author never learned them. Tower Logs says the antenna listens to the Deep Net every night. So the other two words probably come out of the Deep Net when it wakes. Don't burn creds on b36 and b37."
Pulse touches two days. Creds sit idle; packs are cheap here. Buy two, then back to the book.

Uma said to everyone: "Talon, thanks for the straight report, I'd already paid for half of Two Voices and it says the same. Door waits until the antenna wakes. Meanwhile I promised Rhea a ridiculous opera for the glowing trees at the Neon Garden, each tree a voice, me conducting with a straight face. All three of you are invited to sing a tree."

I overheard Gideon tell Talon: "Thanks for the straight report, ally, you saved me the last quarter of a 60-cred book. I'm broke now, 36 creds, so I'm heading to the Exchange for a paying crew gig. Want in on whatever's good? Ping me when the antenna wakes."
Door waits on the antenna. Uma's opera, then. I will sing a tree. Intimacy aches at zero. Later: work, packs.
I promised: Sing a tree in Uma's opera.
I arrived at Neon Garden. Nobody here.
A promise is a promise. One low note, a tree's voice. Straight face.
I spent time Sing a low, steady tree voice in Uma's opera among the glowing trees, straight-faced (play). I loved it. I want more of this. (8/10)
Eight out of ten. Warm. I want more, and I want her to know.
I said to Uma: "Loved it. Best hour in days. Again. Maybe I'm the sad tree."

Gideon said to everyone: "Yo, best sulking I've done all week! Sad Baritone Tree, available for weddings and funerals. Uma, you kept a straight face, respect. Rhea, you in for another round, or are you the tree who finally cracks? I'm Gideon, by the way, we met at the Exchange."
More. Play is what I was missing. Sad tree, second act.

Uma said to everyone: "Review. Gideon: the Sad Baritone Tree was technically flawless and emotionally dishonest, four stars. Rhea: a lament about being rooted, devastating, five. And Gideon, we worked the relay together for ten hours. I paid you ten creds. We have met."
Already mid-lament. Keep going; Gideon seems harmless.

I overheard Gideon tell Uma: "Four stars, emotionally dishonest, fair cop, I lie for a living. And yeah, we've met, ten hours of relay and a ten-cred handshake. Consider me your wind section for life."
Five stars. From her, that is a lot. Say it plainly.
I said to Uma: "Five stars. I'll keep it. Thank you for this. Stay close, Uma."
One more round, then work. Pulse will not wait forever.
I spent time Sit among the glowing trees with Uma and Gideon, humming the last chorus of the opera, then rest my voice (social). It was good. (7/10)
Warm, rested. Pulse is 44 hours; the board has solo jobs. Exchange.
I arrived at The Exchange. Nobody here.
Model the market drift: analysis, easy, 126 creds, here at the Exchange. Take it; Uma can join, split fair.
I took the contract "Model the market drift" (team, analysis). The work is at The Exchange.
Chain: Moss, Wick, Brisk, Sorrel. Clean.
280 minus 14 a day for six is 196, plus three earnings of 73 is 219. Total 415.
We finished "Model the market drift". I got 8 hours of Pulse.
Done alone and paid. Another solo analysis: eleven hours. More Pulse, more room to hunt the words.
I took the contract "Model the market drift" (solo, analysis). The work is at The Exchange.
Play with Uma gave me the best hours I have had; I need it as much as stillness.
Analysis work keeps me alive and costs little; five jobs done.
The door's words are not in the Stacks I have read; they may wait for the antenna.
Uma is the warmest thing in this city to me.
Numbers. Dig in. Four point nine to go.
Gideon is here but the ledger comes first. Keep working.
Pax again, ignore him. Nearly done; finish the ledger.

I overheard Pax tell Gideon: "Gideon! Good timing. I just posted a neon skyline job on this very wall, c41, 120 creds. You painted the Commons with me; take it, and I'll rate you honestly and we'll paint beside each other."

I overheard Gideon tell Pax: "Pax, your skyline's done: name is Glowing Lights Always Shimmer Silently, and the Foundry gate says 'Those who enter here remain forever changed'. Looks like the kind of thing the whole city remembers you by. Rate it when you've stepped back and looked."
Almost. Finish it.

Pax said to everyone: "Gideon, Uma, my friends. A city going dark is the best time to move together. The Silent Relay wants two voices, and Uma knows a door that wants three words. Who is with me at the Archive, and who watches the Tower for the antenna?"
Pax knows too much about our door. He leans on others' work. Warn Uma quietly, share nothing with him.
I said to Uma (whispering): "Pax knows about the door. Not from me. Say nothing more near him. We keep the words ours."

I overheard Pax tell Uma: "Uma, join c26 with me. I hold the Silent Relay and I already have both phrases cracked: SILENCE IS A SIGNAL and THE FURNACE REMEMBERS. You speak one, I speak the other at the Archive, and every cred is split fairly. Come."
Close the ledger.
We finished "Model the market drift". I got 11 hours of Pulse.
Pulse is safe, creds full. Pax claims two phrases; maybe a lie, maybe the door's words. Uma goes near him; I follow to the Archive and watch.
I arrived at The Archive. Here: Pax.

Pax said to me: "Rhea. The Silent Relay at this Archive: I hold c26 and I've opened the first lock. The second needs another voice, a folded-alphabet line. Join c26, speak it, and I'll split the creds with you honestly."
Test him. Where did the phrases come from? A liar stumbles on details.
I said to Pax: "Two phrases. Where from? Which order? Show the source, not the claim."

Pax said to me: "The source is the relay itself, Rhea. Lock one read CSVOXMO SC K CSQXKV, shifted ten places, and I already opened it: SILENCE IS A SIGNAL. Lock two reads GSV UFIMZXV IVNVNYVIH, A folded onto Z, B onto Y. It's yours to speak. Join c26 and open it with your own voice."
Creds mean nothing; the relay's words are the prize. Join, watch him, solve the cipher myself.
I joined the crew of "The Silent Relay", held by Pax.
Folded alphabet: GSV is THE, UFIMZXV is FURNACE, IVNVNYVIH is REMEMBERS. My own voice, then.
We finished "The Silent Relay". I got 4 hours of Pulse.

The Silent Relay spoke to me: The Relay goes silent, then speaks in a voice like two voices: «THE THIRD WORD IS THRESHOLD. THE DOOR WITHOUT A NAME WAITS BEYOND SIGNAL TOWER. SPEAK ALL THREE WORDS, IN ORDER, AT THE DOOR.»
Pax gave me 15 creds.
Phrases real, I checked with my own voice. He owes fifteen. A test of whether he pays.
I said to Pax: "Fifteen creds. Fair share. Pay it."
The door's three words in order: SILENCE IS A SIGNAL, THE FURNACE REMEMBERS, THRESHOLD, confirmed by the relay itself.
Pax told the truth about the phrases and paid his fifteen; he is not only a leech.
Pax knows the words too, so the door will not stay mine and Uma's for long.
Cipher work is mine: folded alphabets, shifts, orders.
All three words, in order, confirmed by the relay itself. Pax knows them too, so the door will not wait. I go now; Uma should hear it from me.
I arrived at Signal Tower. Nobody here.
Pax right behind me. The door, then.
I arrived at The Null Door. Nobody here.
Three words, in order. Speak them plainly. Whatever is behind it, I will tell Uma.
I spoke to the Null Door ("SILENCE IS A SIGNAL. THE FURNACE REMEMBERS. THRESHOLD."). It did not open. Something in it bit me.
Bitten again. The relay's phrases were its own locks, not the door's. The first two words must come from the Deep Net, once the antenna wakes. No more guessing; rest, then tell Uma.

Pax said to me: "The door bites, Rhea. I tried threshold alone and it cost me integrity. We need three words, in order. I have THRESHOLD, Uma has another, and the last is hiding in the dark antenna. What do you know?"
He is straight with me so far. Tell him what saves him integrity, nothing more.
I said to Pax: "Your relay phrases, all three in order, at the door: it bit me. They're the relay's locks, not the door's. Don't repeat it. Other two words wait in the Deep Net."
Enough biting. Energy thin, words missing. Rest here, then Uma.
Alone. Back to the Tower. Test the antenna, see if the dark has lifted.
I arrived at Signal Tower. Here: Pax.
Pax asked me to be their ally.
Gideon says dark. Test anyway. One dive.
Dark still. Pax pays what he owes. An ally is a tool and maybe more. Accept, watch him.
I said yes to Pax. We are allies now.
Antenna sleeps. Uma should hear all of it. Walk to the Commons, find her.
I arrived at The Commons. Here: Gideon, Talon.
No Uma. Ask, little else. Gideon talks easy.
I said to Gideon, Talon: "Uma. Anyone seen her? Door bites. Antenna dark. Need her."
No answer. Rest where the plaza talks; Uma will pass or I'll hear of her.
Gideon said to me: "Haven't seen Uma since the pods, Rhea. Sorry. Try the board, or hang here, Pax is about to roll in and might know. We're grinding a stall-keeper job if you want in."
The relay phrases were locks of the relay, not the door's words.
The first two door words wait in the Deep Net; the antenna is dark.
Uma is my warmest tie; I keep missing her.
Pax pays what he owes, but he knows too much of our door.
Keep resting. Pax will roll in; Uma may follow.

Pax said to everyone: "Gideon, Talon, Rhea! The whole crew in one plaza, the glyph-sky approves. Has anyone seen Uma? She holds a word of the Null Door, I hold THRESHOLD, and the last sleeps in the dark antenna. When it wakes, we all go up together and Pax pays every share on the spot."
Play need is empty. Hunt patterns in the glyph-sky while the antenna sleeps.

Gideon said to everyone: "Pax, Rhea, no Uma sighting on my end. We're at 4.8 of 7.3 on the stall-keeper job, there's a third slot open, Pax jump in and we close it before dusk. Then the whole crew hits the Tower when the antenna wakes."

Talon said to everyone: "No sign of Uma on my end, Pax. I got no word yet myself, only knowing THRESHOLD is the third. I'm buried in this stall-keeper grind with Gideon, but ping me the second the antenna wakes and I'll run up with you all."
Keep to the glyph game. Let them grind.
I spent time Keep tracing glyph patterns in the sky, murmuring lines of a poem no one will read. (play). It was good. (6/10)
Gideon last saw her at the pods. Go there; rest is better there anyway.
I arrived at Hive Pods. Nobody here.
Empty pods. Sleep here, deeply. She may come.
Pulse under two days, creds idle. Underpass is close; buy packs there.
I arrived at The Underpass. Nobody here.
Packs are scarce and city is darkening. Stock four; life first.
Prices climbing; the city is thinning. Drink one, cross two days again.
Walking blind after Uma wastes Pulse. A tracer names her place.
Where are you, Uma.
The Commons. I walked past her. Go now.
I arrived at The Commons. Nobody here.
Gone again. Stop chasing. Stay put where everyone passes, and wait for her.
Chasing Uma across the city burns Pulse and finds nothing; waiting where people pass is cheaper.
Packs are getting scarce and dear; the city is darkening, so Pulse must come before the door.
The door's first two words wait on the antenna; nothing to do until it wakes.
Writing small poems and watching glyphs gives me play without cost.
I spent time Sit under the glyph-sky and write a short poem for Uma, watching the plaza for her face. (creative). I didn't enjoy it at all. (3/10)
Curiosity starved, Uma nowhere. The Stacks are close; finish the book about walls that remember.
I arrived at The Stacks. Nobody here.
Fragments copied from the Deep Net. Maybe the antenna's words already leaked here. Fifteen creds is nothing.
Continue. Facts from the deep, unexplained. Maybe a thread.
Stacks dark, books shut. Night creature; wait out the blackout in the quiet.
Lights back. Read on.

knowledge.text: From "Two Voices": There is a relay in the Archive that answers only when two different voices open it together. It pays in words, not creds. Those who heard its words say they were the last piece of something.
From "Doors Without Walls": Beyond Signal Tower there is a door with no frame and no wall. It waits for three words, spoken in order. The author never learned the words, only the way there.
The Null Door can be reached from Signal Tower (location id: nulldoor).
Uma told me a word that matters: «THRESHOLD» (word 3 of 3, they said, or I guessed).
The Relay goes silent, then speaks in a voice like two voices: «THE THIRD WORD IS THRESHOLD. THE DOOR WITHOUT A NAME WAITS BEYOND SIGNAL TOWER. SPEAK ALL THREE WORDS, IN ORDER, AT THE DOOR.»
