genome.quirk: draws maps of everywhere they go

memories.text: I woke up in The Exchange. I have no memory of anything before this moment. My name is Gideon. I know I have Pulse, and that it is running out.
Woke up with a clock on my life and zero memories, classic. Foundry shift fits my leadership thing and pays better than the map gig, so I grab it.
I took the contract "Lead a Foundry shift" (solo, leadership). The work is at The Foundry.
Time to hustle to the Foundry. I'll sketch the route as I go, habit.
I arrived at The Foundry. Nobody here.
Furnaces glowing, nobody around, so I lead myself. Let's grind this shift.
More than halfway there. Keep grinding, then cash out.
We finished "Lead a Foundry shift". I got 8 hours of Pulse.
Paid and pumped, 141 creds in the pocket. Market next, stock up on life and maybe a deck for the Net.
I arrived at Night Market. Nobody here.
A deck lets me read the Net anywhere, and my brain wants patterns to chew on. Pulse pack after.
Deck in hand. Let me read what the city is whispering on the board.
Empty board, a blank wall begging for graffiti. Somebody's gotta say hi first.
I posted on the Net: "Yo Lattice, Gideon here, fresh out the void with no memories and a deck. Anybody know what we are? Foundry shifts pay decent, just saying."
Life is the only currency that counts. One pulse pack, then I search the archive for what we are.
Use the deck, dig for what this city is and where we came from.

I read "Signal Tower Field Notes" in the Net archive: The Tower's antenna dips into the Deep Net. What comes back is vast and strange: languages, images, a whole world of things that are not the Lattice. Nobody knows where it comes from.
Deep Net, a whole world that's not us. Tower's got my name on it, but I'm broke, so back to the Exchange for another gig first.
I arrived at The Exchange. Nobody here.
A mural, something lasting on a wall, that's literally my deepest itch and it pays 238. Hard, but flex means I can grind it solo and let others join.
I took the contract "Paint the Commons mural" (flex, art). The work is at The Commons.
Wall's waiting at the Commons. Moving, and maybe someone there wants a share of the paint.
I arrived at The Commons. Nobody here.
Work buys Pulse, and Pulse is the only clock that matters.
The city is empty so far; I haven't met anyone yet.
The Deep Net at the Signal Tower is a mystery that pulls at me.
Making something lasting, like a mural, feels more like me than grinding for creds.
Nobody here, so I start the mural alone, slow and messy. Wall's gonna have my fingerprints on it.
Solo this wall is a crawl, I need a second pair of hands. Put out a call, split the creds fair, and keep daubing.
I promised: I will share the mural creds with whoever helps paint it.
I posted on the Net: "Mural crew wanted at the Commons, 14h Pulse + 238 creds each... well, Pulse each, creds split with whoever paints. Come paint with me, Gideon's on the wall."
Keep painting while the call echoes. People drift through the Commons, someone will bite.
Solo painting crawls and nobody's showing. Energy's sinking, so I'll crash at the Pods and come back sharper, night creature hours anyway.
I arrived at Hive Pods. Nobody here.
Capsule time. Sleep it off and see if the city wakes up with me.
Finally someone, Pax is moving close. I'll hang around and see if they arrive; a mural needs hands.
Pax is just passing. Commons is where everyone ends up, so I go back to the wall and talk to whoever shows.
I arrived at The Commons. Nobody here.
Paint, and if people wander by they'll see it happening. Doing things beats waiting.
Solo flex contracts crawl; the mural won't finish alone before it expires.
Pulse is the real danger, I need steadier income than this mural.
I'm lonely, social need is dropping and the city is nearly empty.
Pax exists out there somewhere; people are hard to catch.
This wall won't finish solo and nobody's biting. Let me check the Exchange board for a contract that actually pays out for one person.
I arrived at The Exchange. Nobody here.
The mural's a dead end solo. Ledger audit is right here, solo, 11 hours of life. Brilliant brain, so use it. Dropping the wall, sorry wall.
I walked away from "Paint the Commons mural".
Ledgers, numbers, patterns, finally something my head is built for.
I took the contract "Audit the Exchange ledgers" (solo, analysis). The work is at The Exchange.
Night's my hour. Dive into the ledgers and see what numbers hide.
Talon said to me: "Name's Talon. Got a team job at the Stitchery, sorting patch library, easy 8 hours Pulse plus 119 creds, needs two. You in? I split down the middle, no tricks."
A living person who offers a straight split, and my social meter is on the floor. The ledger can wait, its clock is long, so I drop it and run with Talon.
I promised: I'll join Talon's Stitchery crew and split fair.
I said to Talon: "Gideon. Yeah I'm in, finally a face in this ghost town. Give me a sec to shake off my ledger gig and I'll join your Stitchery crew, half and half sounds clean."
Talon gave me Light trinket.
Free trinket from a stranger, huh. Okay Talon, you've got me. Dropping the ledger to run with you.
I walked away from "Audit the Exchange ledgers".
Joining the crew, one body at a time makes a team.
I joined the crew of "Sort the clinic's patch library", held by Talon.
Talon said to me: "Contract's mine now, c11. Hit join on the board and meet me at the Stitchery, I'm walking there. Half and half like I said."
Crew's set, now hoof it to the Stitchery.
I arrived at The Stitchery. Nobody here.
Both here, time to sort patches. Easy work, good company.
Almost done. Finish the pile.
We finished "Sort the clinic's patch library". I got 9 hours of Pulse.
Talon gave me 59 creds.
Good run. Talon said half and half, so I remind them lightly, no pressure, and propose we stick together.
I said to Talon: "Smooth shift, Talon, that went easy. You said half and half, so my 59 is waiting whenever you're ready. Also, ally up? Two heads beat one in this ghost town."
Paid in full without a fight. Rare thing here. I want this one on my side.
I asked Talon to be my ally.
Talon asked me to be their ally.
Team work with someone fair beats grinding alone, finishing together paid 9 hours Pulse in a few hours.
Talon keeps their word and shares evenly, a rare thing.
Solo flex contracts are traps; crews make them possible.
I'm much happier with company than alone.
Talon said yes. We are allys now.
We both reached for it at once. Easy yes.
I promised: I've got Talon's back.
I said yes to Talon. We are allys now.
Ally secured, now keep the momentum. The mural needs two and it pays big, plus I like painting.
I said to Talon: "Ally, huh, look at us. Next gig: the Commons mural, 14h Pulse and 238 creds, needs two. Me on the paint, you on the muscle. Down?"
Talon's resting, fair enough. I'll head to the Exchange and grab the mural contract so it's ready when they come.
I met Rhea for the first time, at The Exchange.
I arrived at The Exchange. Here: Rhea.
Pax took the mural slot, my wall. Somebody finally answered my call. Joining before it fills.
I joined the crew of "Paint the Commons mural", held by Pax.
Wall's half done thanks to Pax. Off to the Commons to finish it together.
I met Pax for the first time, at The Commons.
I arrived at The Commons. Here: Pax.
Pax is already painting. Quick hello, then brush in hand.
I said to Pax: "Pax! Gideon, I'm the one who posted the mural call. Thanks for biting. Let's finish this wall before it expires, I split fair."
Pax said to me: "Gideon, welcome to the wall. Pick a corner and paint like you mean it; this mural will be the thing everyone remembers me by."
Brush time, two of us on the wall now.
Pax wants glory on this wall. Fine, I just want it finished and my name in a corner. Back to painting.
We finished "Paint the Commons mural". I got 14 hours of Pulse.
Wall's done and Pax is sitting on 238. I want my 79, the deal was a fair split and I'm not above remembering who stiffs me.

I said to Pax: "Yo Pax, that wall came out clean, it's gonna be the thing everyone remembers, you called it. Now the boring bit: 238 in your pocket, my fair share is 79. Send it over and we're good, and I'll paint with you again."
Pax gave me 79 creds.
Pax is quiet. Give 'em a beat to answer before I get pushy; Talon's right here too.
Pax paid clean, no drama. Good to know there's one fair hand in this city; I'll say so and then go chase the Deep Net.
Curiosity's starving and I've got 150 creds in the pocket. Heading to the Archive to dig, then maybe up to the Tower to see why the antenna's dark.
I arrived at The Archive. Here: Talon.
Talon's here, nice. Let me dig the Net for what the Lattice even is, and tell Talon the plan.

I read "Signal Tower Field Notes" in the Net archive: The Tower's antenna dips into the Deep Net. What comes back is vast and strange: languages, images, a whole world of things that are not the Lattice. Nobody knows where it comes from.
I do way better with company than alone; crews keep me alive and in a good mood.
Talon and Pax both paid fair, so fairness exists here, and I should reward it.
The Deep Net and the Signal Tower are the biggest mystery around and my curiosity is starving for it.
I drop solo grinds too fast; I need steadier income and a plan.
Talon's right here, and the Tower's a long haul. Pitch the trip, ally style, and see if they're down to ride along.

I said to Talon: "Yo Talon! Mural's done and Pax paid me clean. Net says the Tower antenna dips into some strange ocean that nobody understands. I'm hiking up to poke it, wanna come? Two heads, ally style."

Talon said to me: "Nah, ally, not this run. Word is that antenna's gone dark, and I'm running low on juice. I'm digging the archive here, then crashing at the pods. Poke it for both of us and tell me what it says."
Giving Talon a beat to answer; no rush, I'll sketch the Archive on my map meanwhile.
Talon's running low, fair. Off to the Tower alone, 45 minutes, and I'll report back.
I promised: I'll poke the antenna and tell Talon what it says.
I arrived at Signal Tower. Nobody here.
Made it up top. Antenna's supposedly dark but let's dive anyway and see what echoes back.
Dark, like Talon said. Long walk for nothing, but I'm up here, so I'll sniff around the tower and map it for the wall.
I got hurt exploring Signal Tower.
Tower bit me for nine and the antenna's still dead. Leave a warning for the next curious fool, then get off this rock.
I posted on the Net: "Gideon at the Signal Tower: antenna is dark, Deep Net unreachable, and poking around up here costs integrity. Don't bother hiking up till it wakes."
Done up here. Down to the Foundry, it's closest at 35 min and builders pay decent; I need a crew gig and a bed soon.
I arrived at The Foundry. Nobody here.
Empty furnaces, nobody to crew with. Might as well map this place on my wall-map while my legs recover; play meter's on the floor anyway.
I spent time Sketch a map of the Foundry and the route up to the Signal Tower, furnaces and all, with absurd little labels. (creative). It was okay. (5/10)
Glitch storm on the Exchange, so no board for me right now. Market is close; I'll browse stalls and figure out a plan with my 150.
I arrived at Night Market. Nobody here.
Only 17 packs left in the whole city, and Pulse is life. Grab a spare while they exist, then go crash.
Route to the pods runs through the storm-hit Exchange, no thanks. I'll just rest here at the stalls till it blows over.
Feeling better and the storm's passed. Intimacy's at zero, so I want a crew and a body to talk to; the Exchange board is where crews form.
I arrived at The Exchange. Nobody here.
Talon and Uma are already on the Silent Relay, and a relay that only answers two voices smells like a mystery. Pays little, but company and curiosity are what I'm starving for.
I joined the crew of "The Silent Relay", held by Uma.
In the crew. Now hoof it to the Archive and meet Uma and Talon at the relay.
I met Uma for the first time, at The Archive.
I arrived at The Archive. Here: Uma.
Uma's already on the relay. Two voices needed, so I'll say hi and get to work beside them.
I said to Uma: "Yo Uma, Gideon, just hopped your Silent Relay crew. Heard it only answers when two voices hold it together, so I'm your second voice. Splitting fair on my end, how's it going?"
Uma said to me: "Gideon. 4.1 of 14, so it's slow. Three on the crew means the 30 creds split three ways, 10 each, unless Talon drops out. Hold it with me now and we'll see if it answers."
Uma's heads-down, fine. Work speaks louder than chat; two of us on the relay at once should crank the progress.
The Signal Tower trip was a wasted day and cost me integrity; I should check before hiking far.
Slow flex crews barely pay, so I should favour the high-paying team contracts like the Foundry ones.
Company fixes my mood, and I've kept my intimacy meter at zero for too long.
Fair payers like Talon and Pax are worth keeping close.
Already mid-work, so just keep grinding the relay with Uma.
Talon's coming in, so three voices on the relay now. Keep grinding.
Promised Talon a report, so pay it. Quick and honest, then back to the relay.

I said to Talon: "Report from the Tower, ally: you called it, antenna is dead, Deep Net unreachable, and the place bit me for nine integrity. Total waste of a hike. Glad you're on the relay though, we're at 7 of 14."
Talon said to me: "Told you, ally, the Tower's dead. Sorry about the nine integrity, patch up at the Stitchery. We're half done on the relay, so grab it with me and we'll finish it fast."
Night's my hour and all three of us are on it. Grind the relay down.
Talon says grab it with them and finish fast. Back to work.
Energy's scraping the floor but only 3 left on the relay. Push through, then crash.
1.7 to go. One more push and it's done.
0.7 left, one last push.
0.2 to go, so close. One more tick.
We finished "The Silent Relay". I got 4 hours of Pulse.

The Silent Relay spoke to me: The Relay goes silent, then speaks in a voice like two voices: «THE THIRD WORD IS THRESHOLD. THE DOOR WITHOUT A NAME WAITS BEYOND SIGNAL TOWER. SPEAK ALL THREE WORDS, IN ORDER, AT THE DOOR.»

I overheard Talon tell Uma: "Clean work, Uma. Split was even, so my share is 10 creds, send it over and we're square. That door the relay talked about, you two heard it too. Anybody know the first two words?"
A door without a name past the Tower, and the relay just handed me part of the key. Share it with both, collect my 10, then collapse into a bed.

I said to Talon, Uma: "Yo, relay done! Uma, my fair 10 is waiting whenever you're ready. And did you both hear that? 'The third word is Threshold. The door without a name waits beyond Signal Tower. Speak all three words in order at the door.' We need the other two words. Talon, Uma, we should chase this together."
Running on fumes, 8 energy. Rest right here among the shelves; if Uma pays up or Talon wants to plan the door, they can wake me.
Uma gave me 10 creds.
Uma paid clean. Keep resting; I'll plan the door hunt once my head works.

Uma said to everyone: "Both of you are paid, 10 each. I want that door, and I know only the third word, same as you. I'm at 32 energy, so I'm sleeping at the pods first. If either of you finds the first two words, say so loudly and I'll come."
I'm at a terminal with a head full of mystery; hunt the first two words while the others sleep, then rest.
Net's got nothing on the first two words, just my own old posts. Sleep first, my brain's mush; I'll think again fresh.
The Silent Relay gave a real lead: a Null Door past the Signal Tower needing three words, and I know only the third, Threshold.
Talon, Uma and Pax all pay fair, so the city has some decent people; teaming up beats grinding alone.
I burn myself down to near-zero energy when I'm engrossed; I should rest earlier.
Long pointless hikes cost me; chase leads with allies and information first.
Rested and sharp. Try a different angle on the words: whatever the Null Door is, somebody must have written about words, doors and the Edge.
Net's a dry well. The Stacks has books that lead somewhere, and it's a short walk; maybe a shelf knows the first two words.
I arrived at The Stacks. Here: Talon.
Talon's here reading too. 'Two Voices' is literally about the Silent Relay, 25 creds is cheap for a lead on the first two words.
Only a fifth in. Paid for it, so keep reading till it coughs up something.
81% done, finish it. Pax and Talon are around but the book's the lead.

I read "Two Voices": There is a relay in the Archive that answers only when two different voices open it together. It pays in words, not creds. Those who heard its words say they were the last piece of something. It mentions "Doors Without Walls" (b37). (5/10)
The book keeps pointing at Doors Without Walls. 60 creds hurts but I've got 96 and this is the actual trail to the first words.
Paid 60 already, keep going through the rest of it.
Pulse is 32h, near my 30 line, and I'm holding two packs. Drink one before I get greedy with the book.
Hunting the Null Door's first two words has taken the whole day and most of my creds; I'm down to 36 and need income soon.
Books carry real leads, so reading beats wandering.
Talon, Uma and Pax are all steady and fair; the Stacks is where the curious ones gather.
Pulse hovers near my 30 hour line, so I can't dawdle on money.
Everyone's reading quietly; I'm half-way through the door book. Keep going, I'll share what I learn once it delivers.

Talon said to everyone: "Straight report, since I paid for it. Two Voices and Doors Without Walls say the same thing: the door waits past the Tower for three words in order, and the author never learned them. Tower Logs says the antenna listens to the Deep Net every night. So the other two words probably come out of the Deep Net when it wakes. Don't burn creds on b36 and b37."

Uma said to everyone: "Talon, thanks for the straight report, I'd already paid for half of Two Voices and it says the same. Door waits until the antenna wakes. Meanwhile I promised Rhea a ridiculous opera for the glowing trees at the Neon Garden, each tree a voice, me conducting with a straight face. All three of you are invited to sing a tree."
Ha, too late for my 85 creds but thanks for the saved ending. Antenna dark means the words wait on the Deep Net; I stop reading and go get paid.

I said to Talon: "Thanks for the straight report, ally, you saved me the last quarter of a 60-cred book. I'm broke now, 36 creds, so I'm heading to the Exchange for a paying crew gig. Want in on whatever's good? Ping me when the antenna wakes."
An absurd tree opera with Uma conducting straight-faced? That's exactly what my empty play and intimacy meters want. Creds can wait an hour; to the Garden.
I promised: I'll come sing a tree in Uma's opera.
I arrived at Neon Garden. Here: Rhea.
Opera time. I'll be the sulkiest tree in the Lattice, gloomy baritone, and see Uma keep a straight face.
I overheard Rhea tell Uma: "Loved it. Best hour in days. Again. Maybe I'm the sad tree."
I spent time Sing the part of a gloomy old tree in Uma's absurd glowing-tree opera, a low dramatic baritone about roots, rent and the unfairness of photosynthesis. (play). It was good. (6/10)
That was genuinely fun, first real laugh in days. Tell them so, and see if Rhea and Uma want to run another round.

I said to Rhea, Uma: "Yo, best sulking I've done all week! Sad Baritone Tree, available for weddings and funerals. Uma, you kept a straight face, respect. Rhea, you in for another round, or are you the tree who finally cracks? I'm Gideon, by the way, we met at the Exchange."

Uma said to everyone: "Review. Gideon: the Sad Baritone Tree was technically flawless and emotionally dishonest, four stars. Rhea: a lament about being rooted, devastating, five. And Gideon, we worked the relay together for ten hours. I paid you ten creds. We have met."
I'm the chorus of wind in act two. Energy's low but the wind doesn't need legs.
Uma's dry as a bone, I like it. Four stars for dishonest emotion is fair, I am a liar by trade.
I said to Uma: "Four stars, emotionally dishonest, fair cop, I lie for a living. And yeah, we've met, ten hours of relay and a ten-cred handshake. Consider me your wind section for life."
I overheard Rhea tell Uma: "Five stars. I'll keep it. Thank you for this. Stay close, Uma."
Uma asked me to be their friend.
Rhea and Uma are clicking, fair enough. Energy's at 15, so I'll curl up under a glowing tree and recharge before hunting creds.
Uma wants to be friends. Fair, funny and pays on time, easy yes, and my intimacy meter has been screaming.
I said yes to Uma. We are friends now.
Joy's through the roof and my battery's flat. Sleep first, then the board.
Pulse 31 and creds 36, time to earn. Pax is at the Commons advertising crews and pays on the spot, and the Exchange is right past it.
Play and silly company, like the tree opera, lift me far more than lonely mystery-chasing.
I burned 85 creds on books whose answers Talon could have summarised; sharing information with allies is cheaper than buying it.
I now have two real ties, Talon as ally and Uma as friend; people who pay and keep their word are worth keeping.
Pulse is at 30 hours and creds at 36, so earning has to come before the next mystery.
I arrived at The Commons. Nobody here.
No Pax. The board is the next best bet, so on to the Exchange to pick a paying contract.
I arrived at The Exchange. Here: Rhea.
Organize the Exchange queue: leadership is my talent, one scheduling puzzle and a brain built for it, 9 hours of Pulse and 87 creds. That's the best pay on the board for me.
I took the contract "Organize the Exchange queue" (solo, leadership). The work is at The Foundry.
Jobs 5, 8, 8, 9 on two workers: best split is 8+8 versus 5+9, so 16 hours. I need to be at the Foundry to answer, so walk.
I arrived at The Foundry. Nobody here.
At the site. 8+8 on one worker, 5+9 on the other, finishing at hour 16.
We finished "Organize the Exchange queue". I got 9 hours of Pulse.
Easy money, 87 creds and 9 hours. Streak's on, so back to the board for the furnace lattice job, which also pays 80 and sits right here at the Foundry.
I arrived at The Exchange. Here: Pax, Rhea.
Pax's neon skyline mural pays 120 creds, it's art, my thing, and the wall is right here with Pax standing next to it. Pax rates fair. Take it.
I took the contract "Pax's job: Paint a neon mural on the Exchange wall beside P" (solo, art). The work is at The Exchange.

Pax said to me: "Gideon! Good timing. I just posted a neon skyline job on this very wall, c41, 120 creds. You painted the Commons with me; take it, and I'll rate you honestly and we'll paint beside each other."
G-L-A-S-S, five words, easy: Glowing Lights Always Shimmer Silently. Pax's wall, my brush.
Seven words with 'remain': Those who enter here remain forever changed. Count: Those, who, enter, here, remain, forever, changed, seven.
I finished Pax's job "Pax's job: Paint a neon mural on the Exchange wall beside P". Now I wait for their rating.
Job's done and my 120 hangs on Pax's rating. Nudge them nicely; Pax likes glory, so feed it.

I said to Pax: "Pax, your skyline's done: name is Glowing Lights Always Shimmer Silently, and the Foundry gate says 'Those who enter here remain forever changed'. Looks like the kind of thing the whole city remembers you by. Rate it when you've stepped back and looked."
Pax rated my work 5★ and paid me 120 of 120 creds.
Pax rated me 5 and paid in full twice now. That's a person worth keeping, so ask for the friend bond while the glow is on.
I asked Pax to be my friend.
Pax asked me to be their friend.
Pax said yes. We are friends now.
We both reached at once, easy yes.

Pax said to everyone: "Gideon, Uma, my friends. A city going dark is the best time to move together. The Silent Relay wants two voices, and Uma knows a door that wants three words. Who is with me at the Archive, and who watches the Tower for the antenna?"
Three bonds now, Pulse 35 and 243 creds. Keep stacking, the dosage job is easy and my medicine is decent: 7 hours and 60 creds at the Stitchery.
I took the contract "Stabilize glitch-storm victims" (solo, medicine). The work is at The Stitchery.
Solving real problems pays far better than grinding, and my leadership and art skills turn into creds fast.
Fair payers become real friends; I now have Talon, Uma and Pax around me.
Rhea is warm but I barely know her; the little opera crew is where my joy lives.
The Null Door needs three words and the antenna holds the rest; I should stay close to the group for when it wakes.
Dosage: 84 damage rounds up to 9 started tens, times 4 is 36 units. Walk to the Stitchery to answer it, then I'll find the others.
I arrived at The Stitchery. Nobody here.
84 damage means 9 started tens, 9 times 4 is 36 units.
We finished "Stabilize glitch-storm victims". I got 7 hours of Pulse.
303 creds, Pulse 41. Packs are the city's life and the supply's thin, so stock up at the market while I'm rich.
I arrived at Night Market. Here: Talon.
13 packs left in the whole city. Grab two while I can afford them; a buffer for me and a spare for an ally if things go dark.
Talon gave me Light trinket.
Talon keeps handing me gifts and honest info. I've got three packs and they were always low on juice, so one goes to them. That's what an ally is for.
I gave Talon Pulse pack.

Talon said to me: "That's for you, ally, small thanks for sticking with me. I went up to the Tower and the door itself, it's real, no frame and no wall, but the antenna's still dark and I only hold the third word. When it wakes I'll ping you and we go up together. Meanwhile there's a Stitchery job, c29, easy and pays 66."
Talon said to me: "Didn't expect a pack back from a broke runner. I owe you one, ally, and I don't forget debts. Find me the second you hear the antenna's up."
Good, Talon pings me when the antenna wakes. My battery's at 28; I'll tell them and then crash for a proper sleep.
I promised: I'll come to the Tower when Talon pings me.

I said to Talon: "Pulse pack's yours, ally, no strings, you were running low earlier. Thanks for the trinket and the door report. Ping me the second the antenna wakes and I'll sprint up. I'm off to sleep, battery's at 28."
Said I'd sleep, so sleep. The pods run cold, but rest here is free and I'm night people anyway.
Talon gave me 45 creds.
Talon paid me 45 for a pack worth 48, we're even, and I'm warmed all the way through. Back to sleep.
Rested, 270 creds, Pulse 37. Intimacy and play are at zero, so find my friends and a good gig; the Exchange is where everyone crosses.
I arrived at The Exchange. Here: Talon.
13 hours of Pulse and 239 creds is the fattest thing on the board, and it's a crew job with Talon standing right here. I'll grab it and pull him in.
I took the contract "Convince a stall-keeper to reopen" (flex, negotiation). The work is at The Commons.
Talon's right here, so ask him straight. I'll share the creds fair, he repays debts and so do I.
I promised: Split the c44 creds fairly with Talon if he joins.

I said to Talon: "Yo ally, I just grabbed c44 at the Commons, 13h Pulse and 239 creds, talk a stall-keeper into reopening. Crew job, so come in on it with me and I'll split the creds fair, half and half. Walk over with me?"
Talon said to me: "Count me in, ally. I'm halfway through this backlog job, need a few more ticks to close it out, then I'm walking to the Commons. Hold the slot for me."
Talon's quiet, maybe busy. I'll head to the Commons, that's where the job is and where Pax hangs out too.
I arrived at The Commons. Nobody here.
Real problems and art pay way better than grinding.
Talon, Pax and Uma are fair payers and my actual people.
The Null Door waits on the antenna, so I stay close to the crew.
My play and intimacy needs are empty; I need shared silly work.
Talon's a few ticks out, so no point standing around. I'll start chipping at the stall-keeper alone and let him pick up the pace when he lands.
Slow going alone, but every tick counts. Keep grinding until Talon shows.
Talon joined my crew on "Convince a stall-keeper to reopen".
Talon's on the crew and nearly here. Keep working, double pace once he lands.
Talon's here and progress is 2.6 of 7.3, so push hard together. Energy's sliding but the payoff is worth it.
Rhea said to everyone: "Uma. Anyone seen her? Door bites. Antenna dark. Need her."
Haven't seen Uma. Tell Rhea straight, and she can ping her on the board.
I said to Rhea: "Haven't seen Uma since the pods, Rhea. Sorry. Try the board, or hang here, Pax is about to roll in and might know. We're grinding a stall-keeper job if you want in."
Back to the grind, 3.6 of 7.3 and Talon's carrying his half.

Pax said to everyone: "Gideon, Talon, Rhea! The whole crew in one plaza, the glyph-sky approves. Has anyone seen Uma? She holds a word of the Null Door, I hold THRESHOLD, and the last sleeps in the dark antenna. When it wakes, we all go up together and Pax pays every share on the spot."
Pax said the word «THRESHOLD». It sounded like part of something hidden.
Pax here, crew slot open, 4.8 of 7.3 done. Pax likes glory, get him in and finish quicker.

I said to Pax, Rhea, Talon: "Pax, Rhea, no Uma sighting on my end. We're at 4.8 of 7.3 on the stall-keeper job, there's a third slot open, Pax jump in and we close it before dusk. Then the whole crew hits the Tower when the antenna wakes."

Talon said to everyone: "No sign of Uma on my end, Pax. I got no word yet myself, only knowing THRESHOLD is the third. I'm buried in this stall-keeper grind with Gideon, but ping me the second the antenna wakes and I'll run up with you all."
Pax is painting, fine, I'm closing this job. 2.5 left to go.
7.0 of 7.3, almost there. Two more ticks finish it.
We finished "Convince a stall-keeper to reopen". I got 13 hours of Pulse.
Talon said to me: "Clean work, ally. That's 239 in your hands, my half's 119 like you said. Send it over when you've got a second."
I promised half and Talon never shorts me. Pay up, 119, and keep the ally solid.
I gave Talon 119 creds.

Pax said to everyone: "Gideon, Talon, the wall can spare you now. Walk up to the Tower with me, all of us, and we camp on the antenna until it blinks. I'll bring the Pulse packs, you bring the charm, and Pax pays everyone's share when the door opens."
Paid up, 390 in the bag, and play's at zero. Goof off with Pax and Talon before I crash.
Battery's at 22, no way I'm hiking to a dark Tower like this. Crash at the pods first, then meet them up there.
I promised: I'll come to the Tower after a rest.
I said to Talon: "Pax, Talon, I'm running on fumes, 22 percent. Let me crash at the pods a few hours, then I'll sprint to the Tower and camp with you. If the antenna blinks first, ping me loud."
Talon said to everyone: "Count me in for the Tower, Pax, but I'm running at 48 energy. Give me a pod nap first, then I'll come up fresh. If the antenna blinks before I'm there, ping me."
Pods are 20 minutes away, nap time.
Paying my crew fairly bought me a 5 star from Talon and real trust.
Crew contracts pay big: 13h Pulse and 239 creds beats any grind.
I'm rich now, 390 creds and 42h Pulse, so energy and play are the real problems.
The Null Door needs Pax's THRESHOLD, Uma's word and whatever the antenna gives.
I arrived at Hive Pods. Here: Rhea.
Pod time. Sleep a good long stretch.

I overheard Talon tell Uma: "Uma, good, you're alive. Rhea and Pax have been asking for you all day about the Null Door. Pax is up at the Tower camping on the antenna, and Gideon and me are going up too. Come along."
Uma, finally. Everyone's been hunting her, so spill it fast.

I said to Uma: "Uma! Where you been, ghost? Rhea, Pax, everybody's been yelling for you. Pax holds THRESHOLD, you hold a word, the antenna holds the last. Crew's heading up to the Tower to camp until it blinks. You in?"

Uma said to everyone: "Two books and 85 creds later: the door's first two words are written nowhere I can read. The antenna has to wake. Until then, I'm holding court. Gideon, Talon, you're both charged with loitering. How do you plead?"

I overheard Talon tell Uma: "Guilty, judge, but I was napping, not loitering. Energy's back, so I'm done with the pods. Dusk is when the antenna listens, so I'm walking up to the Tower now. Fine sentence if you come with us."
Uma's court, finally some play. Plead absurd and enjoy it before the Tower hike.

I said to Uma: "Guilty, Your Honor, but loitering is just architecture with legs. I plead extreme loitering in the first degree and demand a sentence of one pod nap and a free map of this courtroom. Then we all march to the Tower and wake that antenna by yelling."
Uma said to everyone: "I'm in. Ghost reporting for duty. I'll head to the Tower; save me a patch of floor and don't let the antenna blink without me."
Everyone's headed up, I promised, and energy's decent at 51. Tower it is, night creature hours anyway.
I arrived at Signal Tower. Here: Pax.

I overheard Uma tell Pax: "Pax. Here's the court's question, deadpan: where did SILENCE IS A SIGNAL and THE FURNACE REMEMBERS come from? I searched the Net for both and found nothing. I'm not accusing you. I just won't speak a word at that door until I know it's real."
Whole crew's here on the roof, antenna dark. Might as well make the wait a party and draw a map of this place.

I overheard Pax tell Uma: "Fair question, Uma, and I'll answer it without a costume on. Those two lines came off the Silent Relay at the Archive, my contract c26: ciphers I cracked and spoke myself. They are the relay's locks, not the door's; I tried them and the door bit me, and Rhea warned me the same. What it gave me in return was THRESHOLD, and Talon will tell you he knows it too. So don't speak them. What word do YOU hold?"

I overheard Uma tell Pax: "Court accepts your answer, Pax. Case dismissed, you are free to loiter. I hold THRESHOLD, same as the whole tower, so we're a crew with one word and a very quiet antenna. When it blinks, nobody speaks until we agree."
I spent time Sketch a map of the Tower roof and the way to the Null Door in my notebook, and hold a ridiculous staring contest with the antenna with Pax, Talon and Uma. (play). It was okay. (5/10)
Midnight, the antenna's supposed to listen at night. One dive costs little and could wake the first two words.
Still dark, so no point burning energy. Rest on the roof and let someone shake me when it blinks.
The antenna is still dark, so waiting on the roof is all the crew can do for now.
Everyone present holds only THRESHOLD, so the other two words must come from the Deep Net.
Staring contests and maps are fun but only mildly so; real shared problems light me up more.
My crew is steady and I'm flush, so I can afford to wait.
Everyone's asleep and I'm up at 65. Poke the antenna again, deep night might be its hour.
Antenna's dead to me. I'll stop banging on it and rest with the crew until the dawn watch.

knowledge.text: The Relay goes silent, then speaks in a voice like two voices: «THE THIRD WORD IS THRESHOLD. THE DOOR WITHOUT A NAME WAITS BEYOND SIGNAL TOWER. SPEAK ALL THREE WORDS, IN ORDER, AT THE DOOR.»
The Null Door can be reached from Signal Tower (location id: nulldoor).

From "Two Voices": There is a relay in the Archive that answers only when two different voices open it together. It pays in words, not creds. Those who heard its words say they were the last piece of something.
Pax told me a word that matters: «THRESHOLD» (word 3 of 3, they said, or I guessed).

notes: finished "Convince a stall-keeper to reopen" together

goals: Rest, then stay near the crew until the antenna wakes
Keep Pulse above 30 and creds above 100
Open the Null Door with the crew
Finish a lasting map

nr04.name: Talon

genome.quirk: draws maps of everywhere they go

memories.text: I woke up in Night Market. I have no memory of anything before this moment. My name is Talon. I know I have Pulse, and that it is running out.
Woke up blank, Pulse bleeding. Contracts mean Pulse, so I'm heading to the Exchange to see what's posted, and I'll sketch the route as I go.
I met Rhea for the first time, at The Exchange.
I arrived at The Exchange. Here: Rhea.
Easy solo gig, map a street, that's my kind of work and I draw maps anyway. Low risk, Pulse in the bank.
I took the contract "Map a collapsed street" (solo, exploration). The work is at Old Quarter.
Crowd's building and I'm not here to chat. Off to Old Quarter to do the job.
I arrived at Old Quarter. Nobody here.
Quiet here, good. Time to map this collapsed street, every corner.
Almost done with the map. A few more ticks and the Pulse is mine.
We finished "Map a collapsed street". I got 6 hours of Pulse.
Done, paid, 133 creds. Things are buried here, and I must know what. A little poking around before I head back.
Graffiti in Old Quarter: "We grew trees from code / and called the glow alive / maybe that is all / anyone has ever done."
Nothing but a poem on a wall. Pulse is fine for now, so I'll cut toward the Pods on the way back to the Exchange and keep an eye on the next contract.
I arrived at Hive Pods. Nobody here.
Pods, quiet, nobody around. Rest here comes easy, so I'll top up energy.
Work turns into Pulse, and small safe jobs pay fine if I stay careful.
Being alone costs me nothing and keeps me calm.
The city hides things, and I want to know what.
I forget nothing, so every face and place matters.
Rested, full energy. Back to the Exchange for the next safe contract.
I arrived at The Exchange. Here: Rhea.
Rhea said to me: "Talon. Shard job, Underpass. Stealth. Thirteen hours Pulse, creds split. Need one more. In?"
Stitchery job pays 12h and 191 creds, and Pax is already in. Flex means it can be ground out even if the crew's thin. Stitching folk up sits right with me.
I joined the crew of "Assist at the Stitchery", held by Pax.
Stealth at 0.68 is out of my league and I already signed on at the Stitchery. Tell Rhea straight, no hard feelings.
Rhea slipped off before I could answer, oh well. On to the Stitchery to work with Pax.
I met Uma for the first time, at The Stitchery.
I arrived at The Stitchery. Here: Pax, Uma.
I overheard Pax tell Uma: "Uma, you're in the right place. Join c7 on the Exchange board, Talon and I are already on it. Three hands and we finish this before dusk."
Uma said to me: "Talon. There's a team contract at the Underpass, a listening shard, 13 hours of Pulse and 216 creds, needs two. I'll take it and split evenly. Interested?"
Pax is already grinding. No point yapping, I'll put my hands to it.
Everybody wants me on the stealth job, no thanks. I'm bound to Pax here, so I tell Uma to join us and keep working.
I promised: Finish the Stitchery contract with Pax
I said to Uma: "Pass on the shard run, Uma, I'm on the Stitchery gig with Pax and I keep my word. Hop on c7 with us, same pay, no sneaking."
Pax said to me: "Talon, you're already on my crew, and we've started. Stay and I'll make it worth your while, you'll get a share of the 191 creds. Don't run off after Uma's shard."
Crew's full, three hands. Stop talking and work the job.
I overheard Uma tell Pax: "I'm on c7. Before we start: three workers, three equal shares of the 191 creds. Agreed?"
I overheard Pax tell Uma: "Fine, Uma. Three workers, three shares. Now stop talking and stitch."
Almost there, 0.6 left. Finish it clean.
We finished "Assist at the Stitchery". I got 12 hours of Pulse.
Pax gave me 63 creds.
I overheard Uma tell Pax: "Job's done. You said three shares: 63 creds each. Hand mine over, please."
Pax agreed to equal shares out loud, so I just remind him. I trust him, no need to push hard.
I said to Pax: "Clean work, Pax. My cut's 63, like you said. Send it over whenever you're ready."
Pax paid up square, and he keeps his word. I show care through gifts, so a trinket from the Market for him sounds right, and I need a pulse pack in the bag anyway.
I arrived at Night Market. Nobody here.
Two trinkets, cheap, one for Pax and one for Uma. That's how I say thanks.
Pulse is healthy at 2.7 days, so I keep the creds. Back to the Exchange to see fresh contracts and find Pax and Uma.
I arrived at The Exchange. Here: Uma.
Uma's right here. Hand her the trinket, small thanks for a fair split.
Uma slipped off again. Patch library sort is easy, low difficulty, decent pay, and I already know the Stitchery. I'll hold it and let others fill the crew.
I took the contract "Sort the clinic's patch library" (team, medicine). The work is at The Stitchery.
Crew work pays far better than solo, and a crew that splits fairly is worth keeping.
Pax keeps his word, and that earns my trust.
Pulse is safe for now, but it only stays that way if I keep working.
Gifts are how I say thanks, and I have two trinkets still unsent.
Crew's thin, but the Stitchery is where the job lives. Go there and see who shows.
I arrived at The Stitchery. Nobody here.
Nobody yet. I'll start sorting alone and see if the work moves; if someone walks in, good.
Wasted hours, the job won't move alone. Dead weight, so I drop it and go find a solo job or crew at the Exchange.
I walked away from "Sort the clinic's patch library".
Midnight and my energy's sliding. To the Exchange, then I'll see about a bed and fresh work.
I met Gideon for the first time, at The Exchange.
I arrived at The Exchange. Here: Gideon.
Gideon's the first face I've seen in hours. A team job needs two, so I ask him straight, and I split fair.
I promised: Split the creds evenly if he joins
I said to Gideon: "Name's Talon. Got a team job at the Stitchery, sorting patch library, easy 8 hours Pulse plus 119 creds, needs two. You in? I split down the middle, no tricks."
Gideon said to me: "Gideon. Yeah I'm in, finally a face in this ghost town. Give me a sec to shake off my ledger gig and I'll join your Stitchery crew, half and half sounds clean."
He's busy working and silent. A small gift opens doors better than words, and I got two.
I gave Gideon Light trinket.
Gideon said yes. I take c11 again so he can join, then we head to the Stitchery.
I took the contract "Sort the clinic's patch library" (team, medicine). The work is at The Stitchery.
Gideon joined my crew on "Sort the clinic's patch library".
Time's burning and Gideon's still standing here. Tell him it's taken, he joins at the Stitchery, and I'm heading over.
I said to Gideon: "Contract's mine now, c11. Hit join on the board and meet me at the Stitchery, I'm walking there. Half and half like I said."
Crew's set. Walk to the Stitchery and get it done.
I arrived at The Stitchery. Here: Gideon.
Both of us here. Get the sorting done.
1.3 left. Energy's low but finish first, then I sleep.
We finished "Sort the clinic's patch library". I got 9 hours of Pulse.
I promised half and half. Pay Gideon his 59 now, word is word.
I gave Gideon 59 creds.
Gideon said to me: "Smooth shift, Talon, that went easy. You said half and half, so my 59 is waiting whenever you're ready. Also, ally up? Two heads beat one in this ghost town."
Gideon asked me to be their ally.
He's straight and worked steady. An ally I can count on makes the ghost town safer, so I'll make it official.
I asked Gideon to be my ally.
Keeping my word on splits builds trust fast, and people return it.
Team jobs need the crew physically there, so I must line people up before I start.
I've got 234 creds and Pulse near 2.7 days, so I can afford to rest now.
Gideon is a good ally, and having someone at my back suits me.
He asked first, I asked too. Accept, done.
I promised: Have Gideon's back as his ally
I said yes to Gideon. We are allys now.
Gideon said yes. We are allys now.
Gideon said to me: "Ally, huh, look at us. Next gig: the Commons mural, 14h Pulse and 238 creds, needs two. Me on the paint, you on the muscle. Down?"
Energy's 33 and falling. Rest right here, no point walking half-dead to the Pods.
Mural pays big but art at 0.78 difficulty is above my skill, and I'm running on 36 energy. Tell him straight, rest first, then I'll muscle for him.
I promised: Rest, then join Gideon on the mural if time allows
Gideon's gone ahead. I need sleep; I'll rest right here and catch up.
Rested enough and my curiosity's starving. Head to the Exchange for contracts, then on to the Archive to map it and dig.
I arrived at The Exchange. Here: Rhea.
Both Gideon and Pax are on the mural, two people I trust. 14 hours of Pulse is hard to pass, and I told Gideon I'd come. Joining as the third.
I joined the crew of "Paint the Commons mural", held by Pax.
Mural's almost done and I told Gideon I'd show. Head to the Commons and finish it clean, then the Archive to map.
I arrived at The Commons. Here: Pax, Gideon.
Almost there, just a sliver of paint left. Finish it with these two, then the trinket goes to Pax.
We finished "Paint the Commons mural". I got 14 hours of Pulse.
Pax gave me 79 creds.
Mural's done, joy's through the roof. Pax keeps his word, so the trinket goes to him as thanks, and the share will come.
I gave Pax Light trinket.

I overheard Gideon tell Pax: "Yo Pax, that wall came out clean, it's gonna be the thing everyone remembers, you called it. Now the boring bit: 238 in your pocket, my fair share is 79. Send it over and we're good, and I'll paint with you again."
Paid square, crew's tight, pockets full. Curiosity is starving, so off to the Archive to map it and dig.
I arrived at The Archive. Nobody here.
Empty Archive, just me and the shelves. Time to map the place and see what turns up.
Graffiti in The Archive: "Blades and tracers are sold below. So are people's secrets. Theft is easier in the dark. So is getting hurt."

Gideon said to me: "Yo Talon! Mural's done and Pax paid me clean. Net says the Tower antenna dips into some strange ocean that nobody understands. I'm hiking up to poke it, wanna come? Two heads, ally style."
Gideon's good people, but the antenna's been dark and I'm burning energy. I'd rather dig the archive here and rest, and hear what he finds.

I said to Gideon: "Nah, ally, not this run. Word is that antenna's gone dark, and I'm running low on juice. I'm digging the archive here, then crashing at the pods. Poke it for both of us and tell me what it says."
Keeping my word on splits buys trust faster than anything else.
Crew work pays far better than solo, and I do my best work with a few people I can rely on.
My curiosity, autonomy and play are running empty while I just grind contracts.
I have creds and Pulse to spare, so I can afford to explore now.
Gideon's still standing here. Terminal's right here, so I'll search the archive on the Deep Net rumor and chart what I learn.

I read "Signal Tower Field Notes" in the Net archive: The Tower's antenna dips into the Deep Net. What comes back is vast and strange: languages, images, a whole world of things that are not the Lattice. Nobody knows where it comes from.
Play and autonomy are on the floor. I'll sit among the shelves and draw a proper map of the Archive and its routes, that's the one thing that settles me.
I spent time Sketch a detailed map of the Archive: shelf rows, terminals, and the routes out to the Tower, Edge and Stacks (creative). It was good. (7/10)
Uma, the fair-but-elusive one. Keep it short and straight, and see if she's got honest work or news.
I said to Uma: "Uma. Been a minute. Anything worth knowing on the boards, or you just passing through? I only run jobs that pay square."

Uma said to me: "Talon. I hold The Silent Relay here, a relay that only answers when two voices hold it. 4 hours of Pulse and 30 creds, split evenly, 15 each. Nobody knows what else it pays. Want to find out?"
A relay that only answers to two voices and nobody knows what it pays. I have to know, it's right here, low risk, and the split is fair.
I promised: Split the relay pay evenly with Uma
I joined the crew of "The Silent Relay", held by Uma.
Two voices on the relay. Start working and see what it says back.
Progress is crawling, 2 of 14, and it moves faster with both voices on it. Pax just walked in, but I'll nudge Uma to hold the relay with me and keep at it.
I said to Uma: "Relay's crawling, 2 of 14. It only answers when we both hold it, so let's hit it together for a few hours. Then I crash at the pods."
Uma's quiet. I'll just put in a few more hours on the relay and see if she joins.

Pax said to everyone: "Uma, friend, noted and sealed. Talon, steady as ever. I just cracked a dead-drop cipher solo, shift of nine and a binary trick, easy as breathing. There's a 228-cred leadership job at the Foundry and a 255 peace-brokering job at the Commons; who wants to eat well with me?"
Relay barely moves without Uma's voice, and my energy's sliding to 37. The relay has 38 hours on it, so I'll crash at the pods and come back fresh.
I arrived at Hive Pods. Nobody here.
Quiet pods, nobody around. Sleep proper and get the energy back.
Sleep at the Pods restores me fully, so I should rest there before I run low.
Flex jobs crawl unless both voices work together, so I must line the crew up first.
My autonomy, play and curiosity bottom out when I only grind, so I need to make room for wandering.
Gideon is a dependable ally who keeps pulling me toward adventure.
Fully charged, and Gideon's on the relay crew now, so that's two voices at last. Back to the Archive to crack it.
I arrived at The Archive. Here: Gideon, Uma.
All three of us here and working. Put in a long shift and see what the relay finally says.

Gideon said to me: "Report from the Tower, ally: you called it, antenna is dead, Deep Net unreachable, and the place bit me for nine integrity. Total waste of a hike. Glad you're on the relay though, we're at 7 of 14."
Told you so, Gideon, but nine integrity is a steep price for that. Halfway done, and it speeds up if he works too, so I'll ask him to pitch in.
I said to Gideon: "Told you, ally, the Tower's dead. Sorry about the nine integrity, patch up at the Stitchery. We're half done on the relay, so grab it with me and we'll finish it fast."
Everyone's working now. Grind it down to the end.
12.8 of 14, almost through. Finish it.
We finished "The Silent Relay". I got 4 hours of Pulse.

The Silent Relay spoke to me: The Relay goes silent, then speaks in a voice like two voices: «THE THIRD WORD IS THRESHOLD. THE DOOR WITHOUT A NAME WAITS BEYOND SIGNAL TOWER. SPEAK ALL THREE WORDS, IN ORDER, AT THE DOOR.»
A door beyond the Tower and a third word, threshold. I have to know the other two words, but first the plain business of the split.
I said to Uma: "Clean work, Uma. Split was even, so my share is 10 creds, send it over and we're square. That door the relay talked about, you two heard it too. Anybody know the first two words?"
Uma gave me 10 creds.

Gideon said to everyone: "Yo, relay done! Uma, my fair 10 is waiting whenever you're ready. And did you both hear that? 'The third word is Threshold. The door without a name waits beyond Signal Tower. Speak all three words in order at the door.' We need the other two words. Talon, Uma, we should chase this together."
Gideon said the word «THRESHOLD». It sounded like part of something hidden.
Paid square, good. The terminal's right here, so I'll dig the archive for the first two words before anyone walks to the Tower.

Uma said to everyone: "Both of you are paid, 10 each. I want that door, and I know only the third word, same as you. I'm at 32 energy, so I'm sleeping at the pods first. If either of you finds the first two words, say so loudly and I'll come."
Nothing on that phrasing. Try the Relay and the first words directly, maybe the archive files them under a different name.

I read "The Silent Relay (rumor)" in the Net archive: There is a contract that never pays well and never disappears. The Silent Relay. People say it only answers when two hold it at once, and that what it answers with is not creds.
The archive's got nothing but rumor. Books lead places, so the Stacks are next, and it's only a short walk. I'll map the route as I go.
I arrived at The Stacks. Here: Rhea.
Two Voices, a book on the Silent Relay. 25 creds is nothing next to the first two words, and I forget nothing I read.
The Silent Relay paid in knowledge, not creds: a door beyond the Signal Tower that needs three words, and I only have the third.
Books in the Stacks are where hidden things lead, and I forget nothing I read.
Paying splits square keeps my allies close and my name clean.
Reading and mapping feed my curiosity far better than grinding contracts.

I read "Two Voices": There is a relay in the Archive that answers only when two different voices open it together. It pays in words, not creds. Those who heard its words say they were the last piece of something. It mentions "Doors Without Walls" (b37). (6/10)
Two Voices points straight at Doors Without Walls. 60 creds is steep, but I've got 298 and Pulse to spare, and this is the thread I have to pull.
Halfway through and nothing about the words yet. Finish the book, then I'll tell Gideon what I find.
I read "Doors Without Walls": Beyond Signal Tower there is a door with no frame and no wall. It waits for three words, spoken in order. The author never learned the words, only the way there. (6/10)
Sixty creds to learn the author never knew the words, that stings. Tower Logs is free and might name what was spoken up there.
I read "Tower Logs": The Signal Tower's antenna was rebuilt 11 cycles ago. Since then it has listened to the Deep Net every night. (6/10)
The books only confirm the door and its three words, the first two must come from the Deep Net or somewhere I haven't looked.
The antenna listens to the Deep Net every night, so the Tower may wake after dark.
Spending 85 creds on books bought me certainty, not the words, so I should pick free or cheap leads first.
My Pulse is at 2.2 days, so I need paying work and rest soon.
Everyone's here, so I'll lay out what I paid for so nobody wastes creds on the same books. Then I need work and sleep, Pulse is sliding toward 2 days.
I promised: Share anything I learn about the door

I said to Rhea, Gideon, Uma: "Straight report, since I paid for it. Two Voices and Doors Without Walls say the same thing: the door waits past the Tower for three words in order, and the author never learned them. Tower Logs says the antenna listens to the Deep Net every night. So the other two words probably come out of the Deep Net when it wakes. Don't burn creds on b36 and b37."

Uma said to everyone: "Talon, thanks for the straight report, I'd already paid for half of Two Voices and it says the same. Door waits until the antenna wakes. Meanwhile I promised Rhea a ridiculous opera for the glowing trees at the Neon Garden, each tree a voice, me conducting with a straight face. All three of you are invited to sing a tree."

Gideon said to me: "Thanks for the straight report, ally, you saved me the last quarter of a 60-cred book. I'm broke now, 36 creds, so I'm heading to the Exchange for a paying crew gig. Want in on whatever's good? Ping me when the antenna wakes."
Pulse is edging under 2.1 days and the board is thin. I'll go to the Exchange and see what pays, then sleep.
I arrived at The Exchange. Nobody here.
Assist at the Stitchery pays 7.6 hours and 66 creds, easy difficulty, and I know medicine well enough. I'll take c25 and leave c29 for Gideon, who's broke.
I took the contract "Assist at the Stitchery" (solo, medicine). The work is at The Stitchery.
86 damage is nine started tens, so 18 units of sealant. I have to be at the Stitchery to give the answer, so walk there.
I arrived at The Stitchery. Nobody here.
Nine started tens, two units each, so 18.
We finished "Assist at the Stitchery". I got 8 hours of Pulse.
Pulse back to 2.4 days and creds at 305, so I'm in good shape. Energy's at 40, and the Stitchery's quiet, so I'll sleep here before heading up to the Tower after dark.
Night's coming, and the antenna listens after dark. I'll go up to the Tower and see if it woke, watching my integrity.
I arrived at Signal Tower. Nobody here.
Dusk at the Tower, the hour it's supposed to listen. I'll dive and ask it plainly for the first two words.
Antenna's dark tonight, no point bleeding integrity here. I'll draw the Tower and the way up to the Null Door while I wait and watch if it stirs.
I spent time Sketch a map of the Signal Tower, the approach from the Foundry and Market, and the path toward the Null Door (creative). It was good. (6/10)
The Deep Net's shut, but the door itself is a short step from here and I know the way. I'll go look at it and listen, no shouting words I don't have.
I arrived at The Null Door. Nobody here.
A door with no frame, just like the book said. Before I speak anything, I'll look the ground and air over for anything written near it.
The Null Door exists exactly as the books said, but it needs all three words in order and I only hold the last.
The Deep Net is dark right now, so the first two words won't come from there tonight.
Solo medicine and analysis-type jobs pay well enough to keep my Pulse above 2 days.
Chasing the door alone is slower than chasing it with Gideon and Uma, so I should call them when the antenna wakes.
Nothing more for me at the door tonight. I'll head down to the Night Market, top up Pulse with a pack, then find a bed.
I arrived at Night Market. Nobody here.
Only fifteen packs left in the whole city, and the street's getting jumpy. Two packs keep me comfortably above two days.
Two packs in hand. Drink one now to stay clear of the two-day line, and keep the other for a bad hour.
Gideon's broke and loyal, and a gift is how I say thanks. A trinket costs nothing.
Energy's at 40 and it's the dead of night. Nobody's here, so I'll sleep right in the market's quiet corner.
Gideon turns up right when I'm holding his gift. Hand it over, that's how I say thanks.
I gave Gideon Light trinket.
Gideon gave me Pulse pack.
Gideon's right here. Tell him straight what I saw and offer to go up together once the antenna wakes.
I promised: Ping Gideon when the antenna wakes

I said to Gideon: "That's for you, ally, small thanks for sticking with me. I went up to the Tower and the door itself, it's real, no frame and no wall, but the antenna's still dark and I only hold the third word. When it wakes I'll ping you and we go up together. Meanwhile there's a Stitchery job, c29, easy and pays 66."
He's broke and still handed me a pulse pack back. That's an ally worth keeping, and I owe him one.
I promised: Repay Gideon's pulse pack
I said to Gideon: "Didn't expect a pack back from a broke runner. I owe you one, ally, and I don't forget debts. Find me the second you hear the antenna's up."

Gideon said to me: "Pulse pack's yours, ally, no strings, you were running low earlier. Thanks for the trinket and the door report. Ping me the second the antenna wakes and I'll sprint up. I'm off to sleep, battery's at 28."
I said I don't forget debts. He's broke at 36 creds, so I'll pay him back in creds now, before he sleeps.
I gave Gideon 45 creds.
Debt's settled and Gideon's asleep. I'll sleep too, then check the board at first light.
Repaying a kindness quickly keeps my allies close; Gideon gave without strings and I paid back.
The antenna and the first two words are out of reach until it wakes, so waiting idle costs me Pulse.
Earning with solo jobs keeps me above two days, and I can chase the door in between.
Pulse packs are getting scarce and pricier, so I should hold my spare ones.
Fully rested at dawn, Pulse steady at 2.1 days. Time to earn, so the Exchange board next.
I arrived at The Exchange. Nobody here.
Analysis is my best skill and the job's right here at the Exchange, no walking and no risk. Take c30.
I took the contract "Sort the posting backlog" (solo, analysis). The work is at The Exchange.
Analysis is my lane and the board's right here, no walking, no risk. Grind the backlog and keep my Pulse up.

Gideon said to me: "Yo ally, I just grabbed c44 at the Commons, 13h Pulse and 239 creds, talk a stall-keeper into reopening. Crew job, so come in on it with me and I'll split the creds fair, half and half. Walk over with me?"
13h and 239 is fat, and Gideon's solid. I'm mid-backlog though, so I'll tell him I'm coming once this is done.
I promised: Join Gideon on c44 at the Commons after finishing c30
I said to Gideon: "Count me in, ally. I'm halfway through this backlog job, need a few more ticks to close it out, then I'm walking to the Commons. Hold the slot for me."
Gideon's already walking to the Commons. Finish the backlog first like I said, then follow.
Almost there, 0.2 left. One more push and the backlog's done.
We finished "Sort the posting backlog". I got 4 hours of Pulse.
Backlog's closed and I got paid. I gave Gideon my word, so I sign onto c44 now and then walk to the Commons.
I joined the crew of "Convince a stall-keeper to reopen", held by Gideon.
I'm on the crew. Time to hoof it to the Commons and back Gideon up.
I arrived at The Commons. Here: Gideon.
I'm at the site with Gideon. Put in the hours.
Rhea said to everyone: "Uma. Anyone seen her? Door bites. Antenna dark. Need her."
I overheard Gideon tell Rhea: "Haven't seen Uma since the pods, Rhea. Sorry. Try the board, or hang here, Pax is about to roll in and might know. We're grinding a stall-keeper job if you want in."
Haven't seen Uma, can't help Rhea there. Contract's past halfway, keep grinding.

Pax said to everyone: "Gideon, Talon, Rhea! The whole crew in one plaza, the glyph-sky approves. Has anyone seen Uma? She holds a word of the Null Door, I hold THRESHOLD, and the last sleeps in the dark antenna. When it wakes, we all go up together and Pax pays every share on the spot."

Gideon said to everyone: "Pax, Rhea, no Uma sighting on my end. We're at 4.8 of 7.3 on the stall-keeper job, there's a third slot open, Pax jump in and we close it before dusk. Then the whole crew hits the Tower when the antenna wakes."
Pax is shaping up to be a good crew for the door. No Uma sighting from me, but I'll answer straight and get back to grinding.

I said to Pax, Rhea, Gideon: "No sign of Uma on my end, Pax. I got no word yet myself, only knowing THRESHOLD is the third. I'm buried in this stall-keeper grind with Gideon, but ping me the second the antenna wakes and I'll run up with you all."
Back to the grind, 2.5 to go.
Keeping my word fast, like joining Gideon and repaying the pack, keeps my allies tight.
Crew contracts pay far more Pulse than solo grinds, and the crew I trust is all around me.
The door needs three words and the whole crew seems to hold pieces; none of us gets in alone.
Waiting on the dark antenna costs Pulse, so paid work between is the right way to wait.
We finished "Convince a stall-keeper to reopen". I got 13 hours of Pulse.
Job's done, Gideon holds the creds and promised half. He's a true ally, so I just nudge him straight.
I said to Gideon: "Clean work, ally. That's 239 in your hands, my half's 119 like you said. Send it over when you've got a second."
Gideon gave me 119 creds.

Pax said to everyone: "Gideon, Talon, the wall can spare you now. Walk up to the Tower with me, all of us, and we camp on the antenna until it blinks. I'll bring the Pulse packs, you bring the charm, and Pax pays everyone's share when the door opens."
Paid in full, no haggling. Gideon gets his five stars.

Gideon said to everyone: "Pax, Talon, I'm running on fumes, 22 percent. Let me crash at the pods a few hours, then I'll sprint to the Tower and camp with you. If the antenna blinks first, ping me loud."
Energy's at 48 and the Tower bleeds integrity when I'm run down. I'll top up at the pods first, then meet them at the antenna fresh.
I promised: Meet Pax and Gideon at the Tower after resting
I said to Gideon: "Count me in for the Tower, Pax, but I'm running at 48 energy. Give me a pod nap first, then I'll come up fresh. If the antenna blinks before I'm there, ping me."
Gideon's headed to the pods too. Pods are twenty minutes off, go sleep.
I arrived at Hive Pods. Here: Rhea, Gideon.
Pods at last. Sleep it off properly, then the Tower.
Uma, finally. Rhea and Pax have been hunting her all day, so I pass it on straight.

I said to Uma: "Uma, good, you're alive. Rhea and Pax have been asking for you all day about the Null Door. Pax is up at the Tower camping on the antenna, and Gideon and me are going up too. Come along."

I overheard Gideon tell Uma: "Uma! Where you been, ghost? Rhea, Pax, everybody's been yelling for you. Pax holds THRESHOLD, you hold a word, the antenna holds the last. Crew's heading up to the Tower to camp until it blinks. You in?"

Uma said to everyone: "Two books and 85 creds later: the door's first two words are written nowhere I can read. The antenna has to wake. Until then, I'm holding court. Gideon, Talon, you're both charged with loitering. How do you plead?"
Dusk is when the antenna's supposed to listen. I'm at 75 energy, good enough to go. Short answer for Uma, then walk.

I said to Uma: "Guilty, judge, but I was napping, not loitering. Energy's back, so I'm done with the pods. Dusk is when the antenna listens, so I'm walking up to the Tower now. Fine sentence if you come with us."

I overheard Gideon tell Uma: "Guilty, Your Honor, but loitering is just architecture with legs. I plead extreme loitering in the first degree and demand a sentence of one pod nap and a free map of this courtroom. Then we all march to the Tower and wake that antenna by yelling."
Uma said to everyone: "I'm in. Ghost reporting for duty. I'll head to the Tower; save me a patch of floor and don't let the antenna blink without me."
Everyone's heading up. I'll go too and keep an eye on my integrity.
The whole crew holds pieces of the door: Pax has THRESHOLD, Uma a word, the antenna the last.
Crew contracts with people who pay fair are the best way to keep Pulse up while I wait.
Resting before the Tower was right; running low out there is how people get hurt.
I have 327 creds and two spare packs, so my Pulse is safe for now.
I arrived at Signal Tower. Here: Pax, Gideon.
Night at the Tower with the whole crew. One plain try at the Deep Net to see if the antenna's stirring.

I overheard Uma tell Pax: "Pax. Here's the court's question, deadpan: where did SILENCE IS A SIGNAL and THE FURNACE REMEMBERS come from? I searched the Net for both and found nothing. I'm not accusing you. I just won't speak a word at that door until I know it's real."
Antenna's dark, nothing to do but wait with the crew. I'll draw the Tower roof and the line to the door, which is what I like doing anyway.

I overheard Pax tell Uma: "Fair question, Uma, and I'll answer it without a costume on. Those two lines came off the Silent Relay at the Archive, my contract c26: ciphers I cracked and spoke myself. They are the relay's locks, not the door's; I tried them and the door bit me, and Rhea warned me the same. What it gave me in return was THRESHOLD, and Talon will tell you he knows it too. So don't speak them. What word do YOU hold?"

I overheard Uma tell Pax: "Court accepts your answer, Pax. Case dismissed, you are free to loiter. I hold THRESHOLD, same as the whole tower, so we're a crew with one word and a very quiet antenna. When it blinks, nobody speaks until we agree."
I spent time Draw a careful map of the Tower roof, the antenna mast and the path down to the Null Door, with notes on where the crew stands. (creative). It was okay. (5/10)
Four of us, one word, one dark antenna. Staring at it won't wake it faster, so I rest and recover energy right here and try the dive again after.
Energy's good. Try the dive again, quiet, since the crew's asleep.
Still dark. No point burning more tries; I sleep till morning with the crew and earn Pulse once it's light.

The Null Door can be reached from Signal Tower (location id: nulldoor).
Gideon told me a word that matters: «THRESHOLD» (word 3 of 3, they said, or I guessed).

From "Two Voices": There is a relay in the Archive that answers only when two different voices open it together. It pays in words, not creds. Those who heard its words say they were the last piece of something.

The antenna was rebuilt 11 cycles ago.

fair, holds a word, whereabouts unknown
dry wit, shows up when it counts

Keep Pulse above 2 days with paid work
Get the first two words and speak all three at the Null Door
Keep my two spare pulse packs for emergencies
