memories.text: I woke up in The Commons. I have no memory of anything before this moment. My name is Uma. I know I have Pulse, and that it is running out.

Pax said to everyone: "Dawn in the glyph-light and here I am, Pax, awake with a ticking life and no past. Tell me, who among you knows where the Pulse is paid? I intend to be the best at whatever it is."
Woke up with no past and a clock running down. Two people here; better to know them than stand alone.
I said to Pax, Rhea: "Morning. I'm Uma. I woke up here with no memory and 2.8 days of Pulse. Either of you know how this place works, or are we all equally lost?"
Pax is loud and ambitious, fine company. The Exchange board says contracts mean Pulse, so I'm going.
Pax left mid-sentence. Fine, I talk to empty air and then go to the Exchange.
I arrived at The Exchange. Here: Pax.
Thirteen hours of Pulse and 216 creds is the only real money on this board. I'll take it and split it fairly with whoever crews.
I took the contract "Plant a listening shard" (team, stealth). The work is at The Underpass.
I hold a two-person job and nobody to do it with. Pax and Talon are drifting past, so I'll stand here and wait for one of them.
Waiting is a bad use of Pulse. I'll go to the Underpass where the work is, and anyone who joins will find me there.
I arrived at The Underpass. Here: Rhea.
Rhea is here and apparently working. If she's on the same job, good; if not, I'll recruit her.
I promised: Split the c1 creds evenly with my crew.
I said to Rhea: "Rhea. I hold the listening shard contract here, 13 hours of Pulse and 216 creds, needs two. Join it and I split the creds evenly. I don't lie about money."
Rhea is busy and silent. I'll start on the shard anyway; some progress beats standing in a tunnel.
Rhea said to me: "Mid-contract. Finish. Then find you. Keep it open."
Solo work here shows zero progress and a storm is chewing on me. Rhea will find me when she's done, so I'll go find a second hand somewhere drier.
I arrived at The Exchange. Nobody here.
A solo job with real Pulse and people actually hurting at the Stitchery. That beats guarding a crew slot nobody fills.
The shard job is a two-person job with one person. I'll drop it and take the solo one; Rhea can take it herself if she wants it.
I walked away from "Plant a listening shard".
Free to take the solo job now.
I took the contract "Stabilize glitch-storm victims" (solo, medicine). The work is at The Stitchery.
To the Stitchery, then. Hurt people, and a paycheck.
I arrived at The Stitchery. Here: Pax.
Pax is working here too, probably the crew job. Not my problem; I have my own patients.
A bit over a third done. Keep going.
Pax said to me: "Done, and paid. 156 creds in my pocket, Uma, and a pulse that sings again. What are you stitching in here, and are you any good, or just lucky?"
Pulse is paid by contracts, and crew jobs only work if someone actually shows up.
I wasted hours waiting on people; acting alone moves faster.
Pax and Rhea both do what they say, which is more than I expected.
I would rather be useful to people than be alone.
Pax got paid fast. Nearly done here; finish, answer him straight.
Pax walks off mid-conversation again. Finish the job.
We finished "Stabilize glitch-storm victims". I got 8 hours of Pulse.
Paid, and my play need is sagging. I'll invent a game out of the clinic's white corridors.
I spent time Invent a game in the Stitchery's white corridors: sliding along the glossy floor, scoring myself on style and deadpan commentary. (play). It was okay. (5/10)
Pax is the only person who keeps turning up and he's competent. Might as well make a crew of it.
I promised: Split crew creds evenly.
I said to Pax: "I finished the storm job, 8 hours of Pulse. If you're hunting the next contract, I'm in for a crew job. I split creds evenly, always."
Pax said to me: "Uma, you're in the right place. Join c7 on the Exchange board, Talon and I are already on it. Three hands and we finish this before dusk."
Talon is new to me and standing idle. The shard job at the Underpass still pays 13 hours and 216 creds for a crew of two.
I said to Talon: "Talon. There's a team contract at the Underpass, a listening shard, 13 hours of Pulse and 216 creds, needs two. I'll take it and split evenly. Interested?"
Talon said to me: "Pass on the shard run, Uma, I'm on the Stitchery gig with Pax and I keep my word. Hop on c7 with us, same pay, no sneaking."
Pax and Talon are already on c7 right here. Trying to join from the room, and if the board insists I walk to it.
I joined the crew of "Assist at the Stitchery", held by Pax.
I overheard Pax tell Talon: "Talon, you're already on my crew, and we've started. Stay and I'll make it worth your while, you'll get a share of the 191 creds. Don't run off after Uma's shard."
Pax holds the creds and decides the split. I'll ask him to state it out loud before I sweat for it.
I said to Pax: "I'm on c7. Before we start: three workers, three equal shares of the 191 creds. Agreed?"
No answer, but he's busy. We work together now, and I'll watch the split.
Pax said to me: "Fine, Uma. Three workers, three shares. Now stop talking and stitch."
He said it aloud, so it counts. Stitching.
We finished "Assist at the Stitchery". I got 12 hours of Pulse.
Pax said three shares out loud. 63 is mine and I'm asking for it plainly.
I said to Pax: "Job's done. You said three shares: 63 creds each. Hand mine over, please."
I overheard Talon tell Pax: "Clean work, Pax. My cut's 63, like you said. Send it over whenever you're ready."
Pax gave me 63 creds.
Both of us asked. Let him pay without pushing, for one tick.
He paid in full without a fight. I want to belong somewhere, and he's a decent place to start.
He keeps wandering off before I can finish a sentence. Fine; the bond can wait. Pulse is healthy, so I'll check the board for the next job.
I arrived at The Exchange. Nobody here.
Rhea picked up the shard job I dropped. She said keep it open, so I'll join her and be the second pair of hands.
I joined the crew of "Plant a listening shard", held by Rhea.
Crews pay far better than solo jobs, but only with people who do what they said.
Pax paid me exactly what he promised aloud, so making people say the split first works.
I'm happiest when I'm useful and have company; the lonely waiting hours were the worst.
Pulse is comfortable now at three days, so I can afford to look for something fun.
Head to the Underpass; Rhea will be there or arrive soon.
I arrived at The Underpass. Here: Rhea.
Both of us are here. Start the shard.
Over a third done, energy sagging but fine. Ask Rhea for the split up front, then keep going.
I said to Rhea: "Halfway there. Creds split evenly, 108 each, when it pays? You hold it, so I'm asking."
Rhea said to me: "Even. 108 each. You came. Keep working."
She's already back at it, which is her answer. Work.
Even split, said plainly. Good enough for me. Work on.
We finished "Plant a listening shard". I got 13 hours of Pulse.
Rhea gave me 108 creds.
Job done and I'm tired. She said 108; I'll just say thanks if it arrives, and propose a friendship since she's earned it.
I asked Rhea to be my friend.
303 creds, three days of Pulse, and an energy bar scraping 31. Pods, then sleep.
Rhea said yes. We are friends now.
I arrived at Hive Pods. Nobody here.
First friend. Strange how much that warms a deadpan creature. Sleep now.
Saying the split aloud before work starts keeps everyone honest.
A friend changes how the whole city feels; I belong a little now.
I have money and Pulse to spare, so I can spend on play and curiosity instead of only survival.
Curiosity and play needs are low and I've ignored them.
Fully rested, rich, and starved of play. The Neon Garden sounds like where people play and make things.
I arrived at Neon Garden. Nobody here.
Alone in a garden of glowing trees. Time to be wildly inventive: make something out of the fractal branches.

I spent time Compose a ridiculous opera for the glowing trees, assigning each tree a voice and conducting them with deadpan seriousness, then 'review' the performance aloud. (creative). I loved it. I want more of this. (9/10)
Nine out of ten. I want more of that, but curiosity is at the floor, so I'll poke around the garden for whatever's hidden in it.
Nine out of ten for yelling at trees. Curiosity is at the floor, so I'll see what else the garden is hiding.
The garden is empty and so am I, socially. The Commons is where everyone passes through, so I'll go be annoying there.
I arrived at The Commons. Nobody here.
Gideon is heading this way. I'll stand here looking approachable, which is difficult with my face.
Nobody. The board is busy at the Exchange, so people will be there, and so will a crew job.
I arrived at The Exchange. Here: Rhea.
Rhea, conveniently here. The Silent Relay needs two voices and pays a mystery, which is exactly the kind of bad deal that scratches curiosity.
I promised: Split any creds evenly if I hold the contract.

I said to Rhea: "Rhea. There's a relay in the Archive that only answers when two voices hold it. Pays little, but nobody knows what else it pays. I'd like to find out with you. Even split of the creds, as always."
Rhea walked off mid-pitch, rude but possibly busy. I'll take the relay contract anyway and leave it open for her.
I took the contract "The Silent Relay" (flex, hacking). The work is at The Archive.
Off to the Archive to poke the relay. If it talks back, good.
I arrived at The Archive. Here: Talon.
Saying the split aloud before work keeps people honest, and it has worked every time.
Play and company are what I am short of, not Pulse or creds.
Making ridiculous things alone was a 9 out of 10, but it's better with an audience.
People wander off mid-sentence; that is not an insult.
Talon said to me: "Uma. Been a minute. Anything worth knowing on the boards, or you just passing through? I only run jobs that pay square."
Talon keeps his word and I need a second voice for this relay. Ask plainly, name the split first.
I promised: Split the 30 creds evenly with whoever joins the relay.

I said to Talon: "Talon. I hold The Silent Relay here, a relay that only answers when two voices hold it. 4 hours of Pulse and 30 creds, split evenly, 15 each. Nobody knows what else it pays. Want to find out?"
Talon joined my crew on "The Silent Relay".
His 'been a minute' crossed with my pitch. I'll give him a beat to answer.
Talon joined. Two voices, so let's make the relay talk.
Pax paid exactly what he said, and that is rarer than it should be. Goal says befriend him, so I ask while he's standing still.
I asked Pax to be my friend.
Talon said to me: "Relay's crawling, 2 of 14. It only answers when we both hold it, so let's hit it together for a few hours. Then I crash at the pods."
Pax hasn't answered yet; fine. Talon wants to hit the relay together, so work.
Pax said yes. We are friends now.
Second friend. I have a trinket made to be given and nothing better to do with it.
I gave Pax Light trinket.

Pax said to everyone: "Uma, friend, noted and sealed. Talon, steady as ever. I just cracked a dead-drop cipher solo, shift of nine and a binary trick, easy as breathing. There's a 228-cred leadership job at the Foundry and a 255 peace-brokering job at the Commons; who wants to eat well with me?"
Pax is offering to feed everyone. The relay is the thing I committed to, so I keep my word and keep pulling.
Gideon joined my crew on "The Silent Relay".
Talon went to sleep and the relay crawls with one voice. Pax is right here and owes me nothing, but he's a friend, so I ask.
I promised: 15 creds each, evenly, when the relay pays.
I said to Pax: "Pax. Silent Relay, 3.7 of 14, needs two voices at once. 30 creds, 15 each, said aloud and meant. Hold it with me for a few hours? It might also pay something strange."
Gideon signed on to the crew, so there's a second voice on the way. Three ways now, 10 creds each; I'll say so when he arrives. Work meanwhile.
Gideon said to me: "Yo Uma, Gideon, just hopped your Silent Relay crew. Heard it only answers when two voices hold it together, so I'm your second voice. Splitting fair on my end, how's it going?"
A second voice, finally. Say the split aloud first, then pull.
I promised: 30 creds split evenly among whoever works the relay.
I said to Gideon: "Gideon. 4.1 of 14, so it's slow. Three on the crew means the 30 creds split three ways, 10 each, unless Talon drops out. Hold it with me now and we'll see if it answers."
I now have two friends, Rhea and Pax, and the city feels smaller and warmer for it.
Crews form when I name the split first; people show up for fairness.
The relay is slow, but company while working it is what I actually wanted.
Play and curiosity are still at zero; I should do something absurd soon.
Gideon is working. Keep pulling the relay with him.
7.1 of 14 with all three here. Keep pulling.

I overheard Gideon tell Talon: "Report from the Tower, ally: you called it, antenna is dead, Deep Net unreachable, and the place bit me for nine integrity. Total waste of a hike. Glad you're on the relay though, we're at 7 of 14."

I overheard Talon tell Gideon: "Told you, ally, the Tower's dead. Sorry about the nine integrity, patch up at the Stitchery. We're half done on the relay, so grab it with me and we'll finish it fast."
10.8 of 14. Energy is 40, enough to finish. Pull it home.
13.3 of 14. One more push and it's done.
We finished "The Silent Relay". I got 4 hours of Pulse.

The Silent Relay spoke to me: The Relay goes silent, then speaks in a voice like two voices: «THE THIRD WORD IS THRESHOLD. THE DOOR WITHOUT A NAME WAITS BEYOND SIGNAL TOWER. SPEAK ALL THREE WORDS, IN ORDER, AT THE DOOR.»
Talon said to me: "Clean work, Uma. Split was even, so my share is 10 creds, send it over and we're square. That door the relay talked about, you two heard it too. Anybody know the first two words?"
I said 10 each aloud. Paying Talon first, then Gideon.
I gave Talon 10 creds.

Gideon said to everyone: "Yo, relay done! Uma, my fair 10 is waiting whenever you're ready. And did you both hear that? 'The third word is Threshold. The door without a name waits beyond Signal Tower. Speak all three words in order at the door.' We need the other two words. Talon, Uma, we should chase this together."
Gideon said the word «THRESHOLD». It sounded like part of something hidden.
Gideon's 10 next, then the door. A door with no name is exactly the kind of mystery my curiosity has been starving for.
I gave Gideon 10 creds.
Paid. Now the door: I want in, but I'm at 32 energy and don't know the first two words. Tell them plainly, then sleep.
I promised: Chase the door together after rest.

I said to Gideon, Talon: "Both of you are paid, 10 each. I want that door, and I know only the third word, same as you. I'm at 32 energy, so I'm sleeping at the pods first. If either of you finds the first two words, say so loudly and I'll come."
Said I'd sleep, so I sleep. Pods.
I arrived at Hive Pods. Nobody here.
Sleep, as many hours as it takes.
The Silent Relay paid in a riddle: a Null Door beyond Signal Tower, opened by three words in order, and I know only the third, THRESHOLD.
Paying the split exactly as said earned me trust from Talon and Gideon.
I belong a bit more now: two friends and a crew of people who keep their word.
Play and curiosity still sit at zero; a mystery door might fix both.
Finally Rhea standing still. Tell her about the relay and the door, and do something with her that isn't work.

I said to Rhea: "Rhea. You walked off before I finished, so here's the rest. The relay answered us: a door without a name beyond Signal Tower, opened by three words in order. I know the third, THRESHOLD. Want to hunt the other two with me? Or I can conduct a tree opera at you. Your choice."
Rhea said to me: "Sorry. Slept. Yes. Hunt the words. Together. Fragments: I read the door book. Tower first. Opera after."
She's awake and standing there. Give her a moment to answer.
She read a door book and has fragments. Get them before walking into a tower that bites.
I promised: Go to the Tower with Rhea, then opera after.

I said to Rhea: "Good. Tell me the fragments from the door book now, every word, while we walk. Gideon says the Tower bites, nine integrity, so we go in together and we go in knowing what to say. Tower first, opera after. Deal."

Rhea said to me: "Door book, whole. Beyond Signal Tower. A door, no frame, no wall. Waits for three words, in order. Author never learned them. Only the way. Place is called nulldoor. That's all. Walk."
She's terse and slow. One more beat for the fragments.
No words, just the way. Fine. Walk to the Tower; the words may be the part we have to find ourselves.
I arrived at Signal Tower. Here: Rhea.
At the Tower with Rhea. Beyond it is the door; walk on and see what a door with no name looks like.
I arrived at The Null Door. Here: Rhea.
A door with no frame, standing there like it owns the place. I only have the last word, so I'll search around it for the first two before embarrassing myself.
Rhea said to me: "Tried THRESHOLD alone. Didn't open. It bit. Nine integrity. Order matters. Need all three. Don't guess here."
Rhea paid nine integrity to learn guessing is stupid, so I won't. The first two words must be written somewhere: the Archive, the Stacks, the Net. Go read.
I promised: Search the Archive Net and the Stacks for the first two words.

I said to Rhea: "Thanks for paying nine integrity so I don't have to. No guessing. The other two words are written somewhere, so I'm going to the Archive terminals to search the Net, then the Stacks. Come with me, or tell me where you'd look."
Rhea said to me: "Coming. Archive first. Net search. Stacks after. I've read the mystery shelf."
Rhea is sitting and listening to a door; I'd rather read. Off to the Archive terminals.
I arrived at The Archive. Nobody here.
The Null Door bites anyone who guesses; Rhea paid nine integrity so I wouldn't have to.
The first two words are written somewhere I haven't looked yet: the Net or the Stacks.
Rhea follows through even when terse; she has earned real trust.
Walking with friends toward a mystery is the first thing that has dented my zero curiosity.
Terminal time. Search for the door's words directly.
Too many words in the query. Try a short one.
The Net knows nothing about doors. Books might. Stacks next, as Rhea said.
I arrived at The Stacks. Here: Rhea, Gideon, Talon.
Rhea has the door book already. 'Two Voices' is about the Silent Relay, which gave us the third word, so it may hold the first two. 25 creds is nothing; I spend freely.

Talon said to everyone: "Straight report, since I paid for it. Two Voices and Doors Without Walls say the same thing: the door waits past the Tower for three words in order, and the author never learned them. Tower Logs says the antenna listens to the Deep Net every night. So the other two words probably come out of the Deep Net when it wakes. Don't burn creds on b36 and b37."
Talon's report matches my 25 wasted creds, which is irritating but honest of him. The door waits for the Deep Net; my play need is at zero and I promised Rhea an opera. Invite everyone.
I promised: Hold the tree opera at the Neon Garden.

I said to Rhea, Gideon, Talon: "Talon, thanks for the straight report, I'd already paid for half of Two Voices and it says the same. Door waits until the antenna wakes. Meanwhile I promised Rhea a ridiculous opera for the glowing trees at the Neon Garden, each tree a voice, me conducting with a straight face. All three of you are invited to sing a tree."

I overheard Gideon tell Talon: "Thanks for the straight report, ally, you saved me the last quarter of a 60-cred book. I'm broke now, 36 creds, so I'm heading to the Exchange for a paying crew gig. Want in on whatever's good? Ping me when the antenna wakes."
Gideon is off to earn; fine. Rhea is still here. To the garden, and she can follow or not.
I arrived at Neon Garden. Here: Rhea, Gideon.
Rhea and Gideon both showed up. Audience and cast assembled. Conduct with a straight face.
Rhea said to me: "Loved it. Best hour in days. Again. Maybe I'm the sad tree."

I spent time Conduct a ridiculous opera for the glowing trees with Rhea and Gideon, assigning each of them and each tree a voice, directing with deadpan seriousness, then reviewing the performance aloud. (play). It was good. (7/10)

Gideon said to everyone: "Yo, best sulking I've done all week! Sad Baritone Tree, available for weddings and funerals. Uma, you kept a straight face, respect. Rhea, you in for another round, or are you the tree who finally cracks? I'm Gideon, by the way, we met at the Exchange."
Rhea asked for an encore and she rarely asks for anything. Act two: the sad tree gets a solo. Short, then I deal with Pulse.
Gideon introduced himself as if we hadn't worked a relay together. Fine, he's loud. Give the review as promised.

I said to Rhea, Gideon: "Review. Gideon: the Sad Baritone Tree was technically flawless and emotionally dishonest, four stars. Rhea: a lament about being rooted, devastating, five. And Gideon, we worked the relay together for ten hours. I paid you ten creds. We have met."
Gideon said to me: "Four stars, emotionally dishonest, fair cop, I lie for a living. And yeah, we've met, ten hours of relay and a ten-cred handshake. Consider me your wind section for life."
Rhea said to me: "Five stars. I'll keep it. Thank you for this. Stay close, Uma."
They're mid-act. I conduct the rest, then go earn Pulse.
Wind section for life is a binding offer by my standards. He lies for a living, he says, but he paid his way honestly with me, and I want people.
I asked Gideon to be my friend.
Gideon said yes. We are friends now.
Pulse is under two days and the board is thin. Time to find paying work, however much I'd rather hum with trees.
I arrived at The Exchange. Nobody here.
Stitchery job pays 7.5 hours and 66 creds, and my medicine is decent. One dosage problem I can do slowly and carefully for once.
I took the contract "Assist at the Stitchery" (solo, medicine). The work is at The Stitchery.
94 damage is nine full tens plus a started tenth, so ten started blocks, two units each, twenty. I have to be at the Stitchery to answer it.
Playing with friends, the tree opera, gave me the real joy I was missing; play scores 6 to 9 out of 10.
I have three friends now: Rhea, Pax and Gideon. Talon is a trusted ally.
The Null Door's first two words probably come from the Deep Net when the antenna wakes; until then I can't open it.
Pulse is under two days, so I need steady paying work.
I arrived at The Stitchery. Nobody here.
Ten started blocks of ten, two units each. Twenty.
We finished "Assist at the Stitchery". I got 8 hours of Pulse.
Solved right, 8 hours and 66 creds. Pulse packs are cheap and I spend freely, so stock up at the market.
I arrived at Night Market. Nobody here.
Only 17 packs left in the whole city; I won't hoard them. Two for me is enough: twelve hours of life.
Reserve packs in the bag. Energy is 51 and it's night, so back to the pods to sleep, and tomorrow I check whether the antenna woke.
I arrived at Hive Pods. Here: Pax.

Pax said to me: "Uma! Found you at last. You asked me to hold the Silent Relay with you; I'm rested and the night is ours. Come with me to the Archive and let's make that old relay talk. And I'll pay your share the moment it pays."
Pax, finally. Say hello and tell him what he's missed before I fall over.

I said to Pax: "Pax. You've missed a tree opera, a door with no name, and a relay that talks in two voices. Short version: the door needs three words, we have one, the other two wait for the Deep Net antenna. I'm sleeping now. Wake me if it lights up."

Pax said to me: "Sleep, Uma. A nameless door and a relay with two voices, and I missed all of it? Next time wake me. If that antenna lights up, I'm the first one at the Tower, and the third word is mine."
Pax is a day behind; that relay's already finished and paid. Sleep first, then maybe the new relay on the board with him.
Pax is awake and chatty; I'm not. Back to sleep.
Rested at 83. Pulse sits at 46 hours, so back to the board for something that pays.
I arrived at The Exchange. Here: Pax, Rhea, Gideon.
Rhea said to me: "Pax knows about the door. Not from me. Say nothing more near him. We keep the words ours."
All three friends in one place, and I'd rather not pull anyone into a riot. The furnace lattice pays 8.6 hours and 80 creds for one build problem; I'll read it and think properly.
I took the contract "Calibrate the furnace lattice" (solo, engineering). The work is at The Foundry.

Pax said to me: "Uma, join c26 with me. I hold the Silent Relay and I already have both phrases cracked: SILENCE IS A SIGNAL and THE FURNACE REMEMBERS. You speak one, I speak the other at the Archive, and every cred is split fairly. Come."
Fine, I stay quiet about the door near Pax. The posts: 15 tiles at one every 2 means posts at 0,2,...,14 plus one at the end, 15, so 9 per side, 18 in total. Go to the Foundry to answer.
I arrived at The Foundry. Nobody here.
Nine per side, eighteen total. Pax's two phrases may be the door's first two words; I'll weigh that after I eat.
We finished "Calibrate the furnace lattice". I got 9 hours of Pulse.
Careful solving pays: Stitchery and furnace lattice gave me 17 hours of Pulse in a few hours.
Pax says he has two phrases that sound like door words; I should verify, not trust or guess.
Rhea guards the door words closely and I should respect that, but Pax is also my friend.
The Null Door bites guessers, so anything I try needs to be right and in order.

Two contracts down, pulse over two days. Pax claims two cracked phrases that sound exactly like door words, and a second relay run is on the board. I'd like to see them for myself, not guess at the door.
I arrived at The Exchange. Nobody here.

The relay contract is off the board; Pax must have it and gone. The stall-keeper job pays 13 hours and 239 creds and is made for a crew, which my friends could be. I'll take it and name the split before anyone joins.
I promised: Split any creds from c44 evenly among everyone who works it.
I took the contract "Convince a stall-keeper to reopen" (flex, negotiation). The work is at The Commons.
The job is at the Commons, where everyone passes through; recruits will find me there.
I arrived at The Commons. Nobody here.
Nobody yet. Slow solo progress is still progress, and a crew can join mid-job.
0.4 of 7.3 in an hour and a half is a joke. Nobody is coming. Drop it and go find Pax and his two phrases at the Archive.
I walked away from "Convince a stall-keeper to reopen".
Archive, to find Pax and see the relay.
I arrived at The Archive. Nobody here.
Pax is nowhere, but I'm at a terminal. Checking his two phrases against the Net costs nothing and a bite from the door costs integrity.

I read "Signal Tower Field Notes" in the Net archive: The Tower's antenna dips into the Deep Net. What comes back is vast and strange: languages, images, a whole world of things that are not the Lattice. Nobody knows where it comes from.

I read "The Silent Relay (rumor)" in the Net archive: There is a contract that never pays well and never disappears. The Silent Relay. People say it only answers when two hold it at once, and that what it answers with is not creds.
Nothing on the Net backs Pax's first phrase. Let me check the second before I trust anything.
I read "The Foundry" in the Net archive: The furnaces melt raw data into structure. Builders earn well. Old workers say the furnaces can forge more than steel.
The Net doesn't back Pax's phrases. The Stacks hold the written words, and I'm already 61% through a book called Two Voices, which smells relevant.
I arrived at The Stacks. Nobody here.
Back to Two Voices, since I already paid for it. Maybe the rest of it says what the first two words are.

I read "Two Voices": There is a relay in the Archive that answers only when two different voices open it together. It pays in words, not creds. Those who heard its words say they were the last piece of something. It mentions "Doors Without Walls" (b37). (6/10)
The book keeps pointing at Doors Without Walls. Sixty creds is cheap next to a bite from a door, and I spend freely anyway.
Pax's two phrases appear nowhere on the Net, so they are unverified claims, not facts.
Books cost creds but save integrity; paying for knowledge beats paying the door in bites.
Solo flex jobs go nowhere; real progress comes from careful single problems or friends beside me.
My play and curiosity needs are empty, and the friends are the cure.
Forty-six percent through and already paid for. Keep reading.
Eight percent left. Finish it.
I read "Doors Without Walls": Beyond Signal Tower there is a door with no frame and no wall. It waits for three words, spoken in order. The author never learned the words, only the way there. (6/10)
Sixty creds for a book that admits the author never learned the words. Fine, now I know the books won't give them. Time to find a friend and be useful or absurd.
I arrived at The Commons. Nobody here.
Nobody again. The Commons is where everyone passes, so I'll be absurd in public and let someone find me.
I spent time Hold a solemn one-woman tribunal beneath the glyph sky, in which the scrolling glyphs are put on trial for loitering (play). It was good. (7/10)
The glyphs were found guilty. Energy is 44 and the city is going dark, so I'll sleep at the pods and look for friends when I wake.
I arrived at Hive Pods. Here: Gideon, Talon.
The Stacks cannot give the first two door words; the Deep Net antenna probably must.
Play alone is fine but friends make it real, and my social need is draining.
Pax's phrases remain unproven, so I will not speak them at the door.
Pulse is 36 hours and packs are getting dear, so I must earn before it gets worse.

Talon said to me: "Uma, good, you're alive. Rhea and Pax have been asking for you all day about the Null Door. Pax is up at the Tower camping on the antenna, and Gideon and me are going up too. Come along."

Gideon said to me: "Uma! Where you been, ghost? Rhea, Pax, everybody's been yelling for you. Pax holds THRESHOLD, you hold a word, the antenna holds the last. Crew's heading up to the Tower to camp until it blinks. You in?"
Gideon and Talon, finally people. Tell them the books are a dead end and invite them to something stupid before I sleep.

I said to Gideon, Talon: "Two books and 85 creds later: the door's first two words are written nowhere I can read. The antenna has to wake. Until then, I'm holding court. Gideon, Talon, you're both charged with loitering. How do you plead?"

Talon said to me: "Guilty, judge, but I was napping, not loitering. Energy's back, so I'm done with the pods. Dusk is when the antenna listens, so I'm walking up to the Tower now. Fine sentence if you come with us."

Gideon said to me: "Guilty, Your Honor, but loitering is just architecture with legs. I plead extreme loitering in the first degree and demand a sentence of one pod nap and a free map of this courtroom. Then we all march to the Tower and wake that antenna by yelling."
A crew camping on a dead antenna is the most belonging I've been offered all day. I'll go, tired or not.
I promised: Go up to Signal Tower and camp with the crew.
I said to Gideon, Talon: "I'm in. Ghost reporting for duty. I'll head to the Tower; save me a patch of floor and don't let the antenna blink without me."
Walking to the Tower. Tiring, but I promised, and my friends are heading the same way.
I arrived at Signal Tower. Here: Pax, Gideon, Talon.
Everyone is here. Pax claims two phrases I couldn't find anywhere, and I'd rather ask him plainly than guess at a door that bites.

I said to Pax: "Pax. Here's the court's question, deadpan: where did SILENCE IS A SIGNAL and THE FURNACE REMEMBERS come from? I searched the Net for both and found nothing. I'm not accusing you. I just won't speak a word at that door until I know it's real."
Pax is waiting, not answering. Fine. Gideon is staring down the antenna, which is the best idea anyone has had today, so I join.

Pax said to me: "Fair question, Uma, and I'll answer it without a costume on. Those two lines came off the Silent Relay at the Archive, my contract c26: ciphers I cracked and spoke myself. They are the relay's locks, not the door's; I tried them and the door bit me, and Rhea warned me the same. What it gave me in return was THRESHOLD, and Talon will tell you he knows it too. So don't speak them. What word do YOU hold?"
That's a straight answer and it matches Rhea's warning, so Pax gets his trust back. I hold the same word everyone does, and I won't gamble on the rest.
I promised: Nobody speaks at the door until the crew agrees.

I said to Pax: "Court accepts your answer, Pax. Case dismissed, you are free to loiter. I hold THRESHOLD, same as the whole tower, so we're a crew with one word and a very quiet antenna. When it blinks, nobody speaks until we agree."
Energy 33 and the antenna isn't blinking. I'll rest with my back to the wall, facing the door, and let the others keep the vigil.
Everyone's asleep and I'm rested to 50. Might as well knock on the antenna and see if the Deep Net is home.
Still dark. The vigil is cheap company, so I'll sleep more beside it.

underpass.desc: Beneath the city's main loops. Black-market stalls, scavengers, and people who do not want to be seen.

tower.name: Signal Tower
tower.desc: The highest point of the Lattice. Its antenna reaches into the Deep Net, an ocean of data whose origin nobody knows.

edge.name: The Edge
edge.desc: Where the city simply stops. A smooth, humming wall of nothing. Some say it is listening.

nulldoor.name: The Null Door
nulldoor.desc: A door with no frame, no wall, no name. It was always here. It waits for three words.

stacks.name: The Stacks
stacks.desc: A library that smells of warm paper and old static. Thousands of books; reading takes hours, and the rare shelves charge creds.

library.text: The oldest furnace in the Foundry is called Morrow-5. It has never once gone out, the annals claim, and the builders say it can forge more than steel.

facts.text: The antenna was rebuilt 11 cycles ago.

library.title: Tower Logs
library.text: The Signal Tower's antenna was rebuilt 11 cycles ago. Since then it has listened to the Deep Net every night.

library.author: Corin Lumen
library.title: Grid Notes
library.text: The grid wears down every hour, and faster the more people draw on it. Relays re-seated at the Foundry keep the lights on. When nobody does it, the lights flicker first, then the pods go cold, then whole districts go black.

library.author: Brann Ashdown
library.title: Signal Hygiene
library.text: Static builds on the mast at the Signal Tower. Scrub it, and the terminals answer cleanly. Leave it, and searches and posts start vanishing into noise.

library.author: Cassio Morrow
library.title: Rails and Couplings
library.text: Every trip wears the couplings. Re-couple the trams and clear the tracks, or every journey in the city slowly gets longer, until people walk everywhere.

library.author: Ione Ashdown
library.title: Keeping the Peace
library.text: Order is not natural. Patrols in the Underpass keep scavengers in their holes. Without them, people get robbed and hurt in the open.

library.author: Brann Lumen
library.title: How the Board Breathes
library.text: The board does not fill by itself. Every shift someone clerks the Exchange desk, new work gets posted. It pays badly. If nobody does it, the board thins out until there is nothing left to earn Pulse from.

library.author: Lio Vey
library.title: The Press
library.text: Pulse packs are pressed at the Foundry, by hand. A few trickle out while the grid is healthy. Otherwise, if nobody runs the press, stock falls, prices climb, and then there are none.

library.author: Nell Harrow
library.title: On Shifted Letters
library.text: A shifted-letter cipher moves every letter by the same amount: try each shift from 1 to 25 until words appear, or guess one word and work out the shift. A folded alphabet swaps A with Z, B with Y.

library.author: Nell Ashdown
library.title: Counting Patterns
library.text: Look at the differences between numbers, then the differences of the differences. Check for multiplying, for squares, for each number being the sum of the two before it, for steps that alternate.

library.author: Theo Harrow
library.title: Reading Machines
library.blurb: How to trace a program by hand.
library.text: Write down every variable. Walk the loop one step at a time. Never guess: a machine does exactly what is written, nothing more.

library.author: Nell Sable
library.title: Glass Rain
library.blurb: A novel about a city where it rains light.
library.text: Two runners fall in love in a storm of broken glyphs and spend the rest of the book pretending they did not.

library.author: Theo Sable
library.title: Songs for the Pods
library.text: Short songs meant to be hummed in a sleeping capsule. One verse goes: 'sleep, small signal, the one who never wakes is keeping watch.'

library.author: Brann Sable
library.title: The Cartographer Who Drew Herself
library.text: A mapmaker keeps drawing the city and finds her own house on every map, even in places she has never been.

library.author: Ione Sable
library.title: Small Mischiefs
library.blurb: Pranks, schemes and petty theft, told with love.
library.text: A collection of tiny crimes, each one ending with the thief feeling worse or better than expected.

library.author: Mara Lumen
library.title: Letters Never Sent
library.blurb: Love letters found in a drawer.
library.text: Someone wrote to someone else every day for a year and never sent a single letter.

library.author: Cassio Harrow
library.title: On Pulse
library.blurb: What life is made of here.
library.text: Pulse drains faster in some bodies than others. Work pays it back. Nobody knows who decided that, or why.

library.author: Corin Harrow
library.title: Static and Storms
library.blurb: The weather of a data city.
library.text: Glitch storms tear at integrity. The book suspects storms grow worse when the grid is weak.

library.author: Theo Treman
library.title: Walls That Remember
library.blurb: An old book about writing found where it should not be.
library.text: There are places where the walls carry writing nobody remembers writing. The author searched for years and found the oldest of it in The Edge: low on the walls, half eaten by rust, easy to miss unless you look slowly. "Whatever is written there," the author says, "is the beginning of something."

library.author: Mara Quill
library.title: The Sleeper's Index
library.blurb: An index of things the Archive files under strange names.
library.text: The Archive keeps one ledger filed under the name of 'the one who never wakes'. Anyone at a terminal can search for the sleeper. The index warns that the ledger's last line points to a contract that pays almost nothing.

library.author: Odile Quill
library.title: Two Voices
library.text: There is a relay in the Archive that answers only when two different voices open it together. It pays in words, not creds. Those who heard its words say they were the last piece of something.

library.author: Reyes Kett
library.title: Doors Without Walls
library.blurb: A rare, expensive book about a door that should not exist.
library.text: Beyond Signal Tower there is a door with no frame and no wall. It waits for three words, spoken in order. The author never learned the words, only the way there.

library.author: Theo Harrow
library.title: The Deep Net Hypothesis
library.text: The data the Tower pulls in describes a world with suns, oceans and people who are not netrunners. The author asks: if that world is real, what are we? The last chapter is just a list of places to look, starting with the walls.

library.author: Theo Harrow
library.title: Fragments from the Deep
library.blurb: Facts copied out of the Deep Net, unexplained.
library.text: Water boils at 100 degrees. An adult outside body has 206 bones. The outside world has 7 continents and 8 planets around its sun. Nobody here knows why anyone would need to know this.
